title: 'You Wouldn't Exist Without Europe' — The Erasmus Baby Phenomenon
description: University Times feature on the million-plus babies born to couples who met on Erasmus exchanges. One in five participants finds a partner abroad; the EU quietly became a dating app.

title: 1001 Albums Generator
description: Daily album recommendations drawn from the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die. Rate and review one a day until you've worked through the whole canon.

title: 2012 Olympics gold post boxes
description: Royal Mail painted a post box gold in the home town of every British 2012 Olympic and Paralympic champion. Meant to be temporary, kept permanent after the public got attached.

title: 2024 Global Crypto Adoption Index — Chainalysis
description: Chainalysis's annual ranking of which countries actually use crypto, weighted by purchasing power rather than raw volume. The 2024 preview leads with Central & Southern Asia and Oceania on top.

title: 2024 South Korean martial law crisis
description: Wikipedia's account of Yoon Suk Yeol's six-hour martial law declaration on 3 December 2024, the National Assembly vote that overturned it, and the impeachment and insurrection trial that followed.

title: 2025 Moldovan energy crisis
description: Wikipedia on the gas cutoff that hit Transnistria and Moldova when Russia's transit deal with Ukraine expired on New Year's Eve 2024. Heat and hot water gone, three dead from carbon monoxide, EU subsidies eventually restarting supply.

title: A Deal We'd Be Likely to Regret
description: 1999 New York Times opinion piece. Paywalled archive page — title hints at a policy critique from the late Clinton era, but the specific deal isn't recoverable from the URL alone.

title: A law unto themselves — San Pedro prison, La Paz
description: Architectural Review essay on San Pedro prison in La Paz, where inmates and their families live in a self-governing community inside the walls. Paywalled past the lede.

title: A Trip to CosMc's — McDonald's space-themed spinoff
description: WSJ dispatch from CosMc's, McDonald's beverage-led drive-thru experiment named after a 1980s Happy Meal alien. The reporter actually goes and reports back on the menu.

title: A Wandering Mind Is an Unhappy Mind
description: Killingsworth and Gilbert's 2010 Science paper showing that mind-wandering predicts unhappiness, based on iPhone experience-sampling of 2,250 people. The study that launched a thousand mindfulness pitches.

title: Abandoned Upstate — gallery
description: Photo gallery from Abandoned Upstate, documenting derelict buildings and ruins across upstate New York. The gallery page itself 404s now.

title: Acquired
description: Ben Gilbert and David Rosenthal's deep-dive podcast on how the world's greatest companies got built — three-hour episodes on the strategy and history behind Hermès, Nvidia, Costco, LVMH, and the like.

title: Acquired
description: Pod.link landing page for Acquired, Ben Gilbert and David Rosenthal's deep-dive podcast on the histories of great companies. Episodes routinely run three to four hours.

title: Aden
description: The Yemeni port city at the mouth of the Red Sea, British administrative hub from 1839 to 1967 and current temporary capital during the civil war. Volcanic peninsula with two and a half millennia of trade history.

title: Adoption of the euro in Bulgaria
description: Wikipedia on Bulgaria's switch from the lev to the euro on 1 January 2026, making it the 21st eurozone member. Covers the convergence fight, the 2025 ECB reports, and the domestic backlash.

title: Afghanistan–Pakistan border skirmishes
description: Wikipedia's running ledger of armed clashes along the Durand Line from 1949 to present, with month-by-month detail on the post-2024 escalation between the Taliban and Pakistan.

title: AI Denies Loan, Refuses Human Appeal
description: WSJ on a borrower whose loan got rejected by an AI underwriter — and who couldn't get a human to review the decision. The automation-of-finance story in miniature.

title: Airstream
description: American travel-trailer brand known for the polished aluminum tube shape, in production since 1929 and now a Thor Industries division. The body lineage traces to the 1930s Bowlus Road Chief.

title: Aktau
description: Wikipedia on Kazakhstan's main Caspian port, a planned Soviet city founded in 1958 around uranium mining and the world's only commercial fast-breeder nuclear reactor, now a 270k-person oil hub.

title: Alaskan Russian
description: Wikipedia on the moribund Russian dialect spoken in Kodiak and Ninilchik, isolated from the rest of the Russian-speaking world since the 1867 Alaska purchase. Eskimo–Aleut loanwords and all.

title: Alawites
description: Wikipedia on the Syrian ethnoreligious group at the center of Assad-era politics. Covers the sect's Twelver-Shia roots, the Nusayri founders, and its scattered diaspora from Hatay to Argentina.

title: Alberta Sovereignty Act
description: Wikipedia on Danielle Smith's 2022 bill directing Alberta's municipalities, school boards, and police to ignore federal laws the province deems harmful. The legal centerpiece of Western Canadian grievance politics.

title: Aldi
description: The German discount supermarket chain, split since 1960 into Aldi Nord and Aldi Süd after the Albrecht brothers reportedly fell out over whether to sell cigarettes. Together they run 13,600 stores across Europe, the US, Australia, and China.

title: Aldi Price Map — Washington Granny Smith Apples
description: Crowdsourced price map showing what Washington Granny Smith Apples cost at Aldi stores across the US for the week of Feb 19-25. Snapshot from a past week; this is the archived view.

title: Algérie française
description: French Wikipedia on the 132-year French colonial project in Algeria, from the 1830 conquest through 1962 independence. Heavy on the economic and administrative scaffolding — railways, the franc algérien, the colonial lobby — alongside the wars and revolts.

title: Alomorfe
description: YouTube channel from Alomorfe. URL-only classification — channel content unknown without loading the page.

title: Alva Cero
description: YouTube channel from Alva Cero, an Argentine YouTuber making videos in Spanish. Channel handle alvacerod on YouTube.

title: Amateurs obsess over tools, pros over mastery
description: Adam Singer's 2023 essay on why chasing every new AI tool is a distraction from actual craft. Cites Seneca and Bruce Lee to argue mastery beats novelty.

title: American Letter Mail Company
description: Lysander Spooner's 1844 private mail service, undercutting US Post Office rates until Congress legislated him out of business in 1851. The libertarian origin story of the Private Express Statutes.

title: AMIA bombing
description: 1994 truck bombing of the Jewish community center in Buenos Aires that killed 85 people, the deadliest attack in Argentine history. Hezbollah and Iran allegedly orchestrated it; the investigation has been derailed by cover-ups for three decades.

title: Amur and Timur
description: Russian safari park feeds a goat to a Siberian tiger; the goat is unimpressed and the tiger befriends him instead. Internet-famous odd couple from 2015 until a fight separated them.

title: An accidental invasion of Costa Rica and other errors made by relying on Google Maps
description: Washington Post piece on real-world consequences of Google Maps mistakes — a Nicaraguan troop incursion into Costa Rica, tourists sent 13 miles from Mt. Rushmore. 2016 vintage skepticism about GPS dependence.

title: Andean Community
description: South American trade bloc of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, headquartered in Lima. Founded as the Andean Pact in 1969, renamed CAN in 1996, and still chasing the customs union it set out to build.

title: Andrés Carne de Res — Bogotá's maximalist steakhouse
description: Eater dispatch on Andrés Carne de Res, the sprawling Colombian institution outside Bogotá where steak, kitsch, and all-night partying collide. A profile of one of South America's most theatrical restaurants.

title: Android FOSS
description: Maintained list of free and open-source Android apps, organized by category with links to repos and F-Droid. The reference for de-Googling your phone one app at a time.

title: Android's Private Compute Core, explained
description: XDA's writeup of Google's belated official explanation of Private Compute Core — the isolated on-device sandbox powering Live Caption, Now Playing, and Smart Reply without phoning home.

title: Announcing Target's Open Source Fund
description: Target's principal engineer Brian Muenzenmeyer announces a corporate fund that donates to open source projects via Open Collective, with internal nomination and voting modeled on Indeed's FOSS Contributor Fund.

title: ANTEL
description: Uruguay's state-owned telecom, spun off from UTE in 1974. Holds a legal monopoly on landlines and DSL, competes with Claro and Movistar on mobile, and started fibering Montevideo homes in 2012.

title: Apache Cordova
description: Wikipedia on the hybrid mobile app framework formerly known as PhoneGap. Adobe bought Nitobi in 2011, open-sourced the core as Cordova, and the project has been quietly shipping ever since.

title: Apple buys Intel's smartphone modem business
description: The Verge on Apple's $1 billion acquisition of Intel's 5G modem unit in July 2019 — the deal that gave Apple the IP and engineers to build its own cellular modems and cut the Qualcomm cord.

title: Apple car project
description: Wikipedia on Project Titan, Apple's decade-long electric and self-driving car effort that burned a billion dollars a year before getting cancelled in 2024 and folded into the generative AI push.

title: Apple's Risky Bet on CarPlay
description: Casper Kessels on why drivers love CarPlay and why the next-gen version — announced at WWDC 2022 then mostly silence — puts Apple on a collision course with carmakers. From The Turn Signal, a car-industry blog.

title: AppleInsider Price Guides
description: AppleInsider's live price tracker for Macs, iPads, iPhones, and Apple accessories across major US retailers. Where deal-hunters check before pulling the trigger on Apple gear.

title: Arab Kingdom of Syria
description: Wikipedia on the short-lived 1919–1920 monarchy under Faisal I, headquartered in Damascus and crushed at the Battle of Maysalun before the French took over. The first modern Arab state, dead in under a year.

title: Aral Sea
description: Wikipedia on the Central Asian lake that Soviet irrigation drained into a desert. Once the world's fourth-largest, now a cautionary tale with a partial revival in the north.

title: Are We Libadwaita Yet?
description: Curated index of 528 Linux apps built with Libadwaita, the GNOME design framework. Browse by language or category, with editor's picks like Nocturne, Wildcard, and Metadata Cleaner up top.

title: Arebica
description: Wikipedia on the Perso-Arabic script adapted for Serbo-Croatian, used by Bosnian Muslims from the 16th to 20th century. Abdulvehab Ilhamija's 1831 conduct manual is one of the canonical printed examples.

title: Argentina Asks to Join NATO
description: AP report on Milei's June 2024 request for NATO global-partner status, pitched alongside the F-16 purchase as part of his Western-alignment push.

title: Argentine austral
description: Wikipedia on Argentina's 1985–1991 currency, born from the Sourrouille stabilization plan and killed by hyperinflation. The ₳ symbol — an A with an extra crossbar — outlived the money itself by about six years.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
description: Jules Verne's 1872 adventure novel. Phileas Fogg and his French valet Passepartout race to circumnavigate the globe in 80 days on a £20,000 wager.

title: Arrest and indictment of Pavel Durov
description: Wikipedia on the August 2024 arrest of Telegram co-founder Pavel Durov at Le Bourget Airport. Twelve French charges including complicity in CSAM distribution and drug trafficking over Telegram's moderation failures.

title: Art Deco
description: Wikipedia's comprehensive entry on the 1920s–30s decorative style, from Paris's 1925 Exposition through Streamline Moderne skyscrapers and the global spread of zigzag geometry and chrome.

title: Asianometry
description: Jon Y's YouTube channel on semiconductors, East Asian industrial history, and the geopolitics of chipmaking. Dry narration, dense research, no face cam.

title: Associated Press
description: Wikipedia on the AP, the not-for-profit news cooperative founded in 1846 that wholesales reporting to thousands of outlets. Includes the AP Stylebook, the Nazi-era collaboration controversy, and the Tuvia Grossman misidentification.

title: Asus offshores 90% of US-bound PC production from China
description: Asus tells Tom's Hardware it has shifted over 90% of US-bound PC and motherboard manufacturing out of China to Thailand, Vietnam, and Indonesia to dodge tariffs. Concrete data point on the post-2025 supply-chain reshuffle.

title: ATACMS — US Army tactical ballistic missile
description: Wikipedia on the MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System, the Lockheed Martin short-range ballistic missile fired from MLRS and HIMARS. In service since 1991, since seen in the Gulf War, Ukraine, and the 2026 Iran war.

title: Atlas Obscura
description: Travel and culture magazine cataloging the world's hidden wonders — abandoned places, weird museums, obscure foods, eccentric history. Crowdsourced gazetteer plus editorial.

title: Atlas Obscura
description: The definitive catalog of the world's weird and wondrous places — abandoned bunkers, micronations, unsettling museums. Also runs trips, food guides, and short essays on the strange.

title: Ausable Chasm — Grand Canyon of the Adirondacks
description: Two-mile, 150-foot-deep sandstone gorge in Upstate New York carved by the Ausable River. Privately run tourist site with hiking, rafting, and a harnessed cable traverse across the canyon.

title: Australian Paraguayans
description: Wikipedia on the descendants of 2,000 radical Australian socialists who sailed to Paraguay in 1893 to build a utopian commune called New Australia. It failed, but the colony stuck.

title: Australian rules football
description: Wikipedia on the contact sport invented in Melbourne in 1859, governed by the AFL Commission. Covers the laws, the VFL-to-AFL lineage, and the indigenous Marn Grook precursor.

title: Autological word
description: Wikipedia on words that describe themselves — "short" is short, "pentasyllabic" has five syllables. The opposite, heterological, powers the Grelling–Nelson paradox: is "heterological" heterological?

title: Automobile Dacia
description: Romanian automaker founded in 1966, acquired by Renault in 1999, and now Renault's budget brand selling rebadged models like the Logan and Sandero across Europe and North Africa.

title: Automobile Drag Coefficient
description: Wikipedia on how cars cut through air — the Cd number, the drag area math, and a table of production-car values from the 1921 Rumpler Tropfenwagen onward.

title: Autonomous System (Internet)
description: Wikipedia on the autonomous system — the routing-policy unit BGP uses to glue the internet together. Covers ASN assignment, the 16-to-32-bit expansion in 2007, and the IANA/RIR hierarchy.

title: Awesome Open Source macOS Apps
description: Serhii Londar's running index of open-source apps for macOS, sorted by category from browsers to window managers. The go-to list when you want a native Mac tool that isn't a SaaS wrapper.

title: Awesome Piracy
description: GitHub-hosted awesome-list cataloging piracy resources — streaming sites, torrent trackers, IPTV, ROMs, scene tools. The standard /r/piracy-adjacent megalist, mirrored as a static site.

title: Awesome Self-Hosted
description: The canonical index of free software you can run on your own servers. If you're trying to ditch a SaaS, the open-source replacement is probably in here.

title: Ayahuasca
description: Wikipedia on the Amazonian psychoactive brew of Banisteriopsis caapi vine and DMT-containing plants. Covers the pharmacology (MAOI + DMT), Shipibo ceremony and icaros, and the modern ayahuasca-religion diaspora.

title: Azerbaijan–Turkey relations
description: Wikipedia on the bilateral relationship between Azerbaijan and Turkey — "one nation, two states" per Heydar Aliyev. Covers the Nagorno-Karabakh wars, the TANAP pipeline, and Turkey's military base in Azerbaijan.

title: Babylon
description: Wikipedia on the ancient Mesopotamian city south of Baghdad — Hammurabi's capital, Nebuchadnezzar's hanging gardens, the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and the ruins later occupied by US and Polish troops in 2003.

title: Bachelor tax
description: Wikipedia on the punitive tax levied on unmarried men, from Augustus's Lex Papia Poppaea through Fascist Italy, Nazi Germany, and Cold War Eastern Bloc childlessness taxes.

title: Baklava
description: Wikipedia on the layered filo-and-nut pastry soaked in syrup or honey. Covers the etymology, the placenta-cake and lauzinaj origin theories, and the regional variations across Turkey, the Levant, the Balkans, and Central Asia.

title: Balcerowicz Plan
description: Wikipedia on Poland's 1989 shock-therapy transition from command economy to capitalism. Named for finance minister Leszek Balcerowicz, who ran the playbook other post-Soviet states later borrowed or rejected.

title: Barcelona's Foixarda climbing tunnel
description: Reuters dispatch on the Foixarda — a disused Barcelona road tunnel that Manolo Sanchez turned into a free, 24/7 urban climbing gym with thousands of holds, now a pilgrimage site as climbing hits the Paris Olympics.

title: Barkley Marathons
description: 100-mile off-trail ultramarathon in Tennessee's Frozen Head State Park, run on a secret start date with five 20-mile loops and a 60-hour cap. Finished only 26 times since 1995.

title: Bayou
description: Wikipedia on the slow, low-lying waterways of the Gulf Coast. The word comes from Choctaw bayuk via Louisiana French — a small stream that turned into shorthand for an entire landscape.

title: Bektashism in Albania
description: Wikipedia on the Sufi order that arrived with Ottoman janissaries and became roughly 5% of Albania's population, with a heavy patriotic-nationalist streak and its world headquarters in Tirana.

title: Berber languages
description: Wikipedia on the Afro-Asiatic language family indigenous to North Africa, spoken from Morocco to the Siwa Oasis. Covers the Tamazight branches, Tifinagh script, and the long arc from Numidian through modern revitalization.

title: Berlusconi's memorable quotes and quips
description: Reuters obituary sidebar collecting Silvio Berlusconi's most notorious one-liners — the Putin vodka exchange, the Monza locker-room bus, the gaffes that defined four terms as Italian PM.

title: Bessarabia
description: Wikipedia on the historical region between the Prut and Dniester rivers — Ottoman frontier, Russian governorate, briefly Romanian, now split between Moldova and Ukraine. The backstory to why Moldova exists.

title: Bhopal's 90-Degree Overbridge
description: NDTV report on the Aishbagh Overbridge in Bhopal, inaugurated with a literal 90-degree turn mid-span. Cost Rs 18 crore; the Public Works Minister has promised an investigation.

title: BMW 1602 Elektro-Antrieb — electric 02 Series prototype
description: Wikipedia's BMW 02 Series article, which the 1602 Elektro-Antrieb URL redirects into. BMW's 1972 Munich Olympics electric prototype, buried inside the broader 1966–1977 02 Series writeup.

title: Book Club Radio
description: YouTube channel for Book Club Radio, the Brooklyn-based DJ collective and party series known for long, dancefloor-focused mixes recorded live at their events.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina convertible mark
description: Wikipedia on Bosnia and Herzegovina's currency, the konvertibilna marka (BAM), pegged to the euro and introduced in 1998 after the Dayton Agreement. Coins minted at the Royal Mint in Llantrisant.

title: Brasiguayos
description: Wikipedia on the Brazilian-Paraguayan binational population — mostly southern Brazilian smallholder farmers who migrated to eastern Paraguay's border departments mid-20th century. The portmanteau was coined in 1985.

title: Brazilians in Japan
description: Wikipedia on the 200,000-strong Brazilian community in Japan, mostly Nikkei descendants who came as Dekasegi contract workers after Japan's 1990 visa rules opened the door to third-generation Japanese descendants. Largest Portuguese-speaking population in Asia.

title: Breaking Down Tasks — Jacob Kaplan-Moss
description: Jacob Kaplan-Moss walks through how he decomposes a project into a task list, using a personal streak tracker as the worked example. Part of his long-running estimation series.

title: Brexit
description: Wikipedia's full account of the UK's withdrawal from the EU — referendum, Article 50, May's failed deals, Johnson's agreement, the 2020 trade deal, and the economic aftermath.

title: British investment in Argentina
description: Wikipedia on Britain's century-long economic grip on Argentina — railways, finance, and the informal-empire debate from the 1820s through Perón's nationalizations.

title: British Malaya
description: Wikipedia on the British territorial presence on the Malay Peninsula from 1826 to 1957 — Straits Settlements, Federated and Unfederated Malay States, Japanese occupation, and the road to the Federation of Malaya.

title: Broadcom CEO admits VMware changes brought unease
description: Ars Technica on Hock Tan's blog post 114 days into the VMware acquisition, acknowledging customer pain after Broadcom killed perpetual licensing, seized the top 2,000 accounts, and triggered reported 500–600% price hikes.

title: Brut FR — French news YouTube channel
description: French-language vertical of Brut, the short-form social video news outlet. Punchy explainers and street interviews aimed at under-35s, posted daily.

title: Budapest Tram 2 — Europe's most scenic tram
description: Travel blog post on riding tram #2 along the Pest side of the Danube, past Parliament, the Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle views. National Geographic called it one of the world's top trolley rides.

title: Buenos Aires Underground
description: Wikipedia on the Subte, the oldest metro system in the Southern Hemisphere and the Spanish-speaking world — opened 1913, six heavy-rail lines plus a light-rail Premetro.

title: Building a 42-inch E Ink Art Frame
description: Eliot Andres builds a 42-inch E Ink display into a custom frame to show generative AI art at Photoroom's office. Sourcing the panel, dithering with blue noise, and a Raspberry Pi controller.

title: Burano — Venice Lagoon's rainbow island
description: Half-day-trip guide to Burano, the lace-making fishing village in the Venice Lagoon where house colors are regulated by local government. Skip the 10am–3pm crowd window.

title: Burma Railway
description: Wikipedia on the 415km Thai–Burma 'Death Railway' built by Japan in 1942–43 using Allied POWs and trafficked Asian civilians. Tens of thousands died; the Bridge on the River Kwai sits at kilometer 277.

title: Buryatia
description: Russian republic on Lake Baikal's eastern shore, home to the Buryats — a Mongolic people whose Buddhist datsans and steppe heritage make this the cultural anchor of Siberian Mongolia.

title: Byzantine beacon system
description: Wikipedia on the 9th-century semaphore chain that relayed Arab-frontier warnings 720km from Loulon to Constantinople in under an hour. Devised under Theophilos by Leo the Mathematician.

title: Cahokia
description: The pre-Columbian Mississippian city near present-day St. Louis, peaking around 1100 CE with 80+ surviving earthen mounds — including Monks Mound, the largest earthwork in the Americas. UNESCO World Heritage site since 1982.

title: Cairo, Illinois — The City That Died From Racism
description: All That's Interesting on how Cairo, Illinois went from a booming Mississippi–Ohio steamboat hub to a near-ghost town, hollowed out by decades of racial violence and economic collapse. Population 15,000 down to 1,700.

title: Candombe
description: Afro-Uruguayan drum-and-dance tradition built on the chico, repique, and piano drums, paraded through Montevideo's carnival llamadas. UNESCO inscribed it as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009.

title: Candy Call
description: Web app at candycall.io, brand suggests a calling or voice service. Page blocks scrapers, so the product specifics are guesswork from the domain alone.

title: Canton Tower
description: The 602-meter twisting observation and telecom tower in Guangzhou, briefly the world's tallest from 2009 to 2011 before Tokyo Skytree took the crown. Structural expressionism in hyperboloid form.

title: Capoeira
description: Wikipedia on the Afro-Brazilian martial art that hides combat inside dance, set to the berimbau in a roda. Covers the Angola/Regional split, the ginga, and the malandragem philosophy underneath it all.

title: Carnaval in Jujuy is a hidden gem
description: Argentina Reports dispatch on Carnaval Jujeño in the Quebrada de Humahuaca — nine days of devil masks, chicha, coca, and Andean pan-flute music while Rio gets all the press.

title: Carrefour Flash — Argentina's smart store
description: WebRetail piece on Carrefour Flash, the chain's checkout-less smart store format launching in Argentina. Industry-trade coverage of the retail-tech rollout.

title: CarSized — visual car size comparison
description: Side-by-side silhouettes of any two (or more) cars at true scale. Pick make, model, and year and see exactly how the new SUV dwarfs your old sedan.

title: Caspian Sea
description: Wikipedia on the world's largest inland body of water, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan. Covers the long fight over whether it's legally a sea or a lake — and the oil underneath that makes the answer matter.

title: CaspianReport
description: Shirvan's YouTube channel on geopolitics, energy, and global power dynamics. Map-heavy explainers with a Eurasian center of gravity — pipelines, borders, and great-power competition.

title: CCCP Reader and Newsletter — Frédéric Chaubin
description: Frédéric Chaubin's reader and newsletter from his 2007–2008 CCCP (Cosmic Communist Constructions Photographed) project, archived on the Internet Archive. Companion print matter to the cult Soviet-architecture photo book.

title: Censorship in Communist Poland
description: Wikipedia stub on the Polish People's Republic's censorship apparatus, anchored by the 1977 defection of Tomasz Strzyżewski — who smuggled out the censors' own internal blacklists.

title: CFA franc
description: Wikipedia on the two African currencies (XOF and XAF) pegged to the euro and used by 227 million people across fourteen former French colonies. The colonial-monetary-policy debate, in encyclopedia form.

title: Cha chaan teng
description: Wikipedia on Hong Kong's diner-style cafes — eclectic menus blending Cantonese and Hong Kong-style Western food, fast service, baked pork chop rice, milk tea. Exported worldwide by the 1980s migration waves.

title: Chang Kong Cliff Road
description: A wooden plank walkway bolted into the cliff face of Mount Hua in Shaanxi, supposedly built in the 13th century by Taoist monks hunting immortals. Sections narrow to 30cm; harnesses now mandatory after the body count.

title: Chase Spend and Get
description: Chase's targeted card-offer portal where enrolled cardholders earn statement credits or bonus points for spending at specific merchants. The Amex Offers equivalent for Chase.

title: Cheran — the Mexican town that threw out police, politicians and gangsters
description: BBC report on Cheran, the Michoacan town where indigenous Purepecha women led a 2011 uprising against cartel loggers and expelled the police and political parties along with them.

title: Chess boxing
description: Hybrid sport alternating rounds of blitz chess and boxing — win by checkmate, knockout, time penalty, or decision. Invented by French comic artist Enki Bilal, made real by Dutch performance artist Iepe Rubingh.

title: China and Brazil's EV Trade — NYT
description: New York Times piece on China's electric vehicle push into Brazil, as BYD and rivals build factories and flood the market while Detroit sits it out. Climate-desk reporting on the new EV supply chain.

title: China's Surveillance of Troubled People
description: WSJ dispatch on how Beijing's public-security apparatus tracks and pre-empts citizens it deems destabilizing — petitioners, the mentally ill, the aggrieved. Inside the grid-management system that turns social grievance into a policing problem.

title: Chips and Cheese
description: Substack publication doing deep technical dives into CPUs, GPUs, and computer architecture. Microbenchmarks, die shots, and uarch analysis from a small crew of hardware nerds.

title: Churning.io
description: Community hub for credit card churning — chasing sign-up bonuses, manufactured spend, and award travel. Companion site to the r/churning subreddit ecosystem.

title: Cia-Cia language
description: Austronesian language spoken around Baubau on Buton island, Indonesia, with about 105,000 speakers. Famous for adopting Hangul as one of its writing systems in 2009.

title: Cinema of the Soviet Union
description: Wikipedia's overview of Soviet film from the silent-era avant-garde through perestroika, organized by decade and genre — Red Westerns, war epics, and the trophy films looted from Germany in 1945.

title: City Street Orientations around the World
description: Geoff Boeing's polar histograms of street grid orientations across 100 world cities, generated with OSMnx. Companion post to the research paper, extending his earlier US-only version.

title: Cliff Young — Australian ultramarathoner
description: Australian potato farmer who won the inaugural 1983 Sydney to Melbourne Ultramarathon at age 61, shuffling 875 km in gumboots and inventing a now-eponymous running gait.

title: Climate Change in the Maldives
description: Wikipedia on how sea level rise threatens an archipelago averaging 1.5 meters above sea level. By 2050, 80% of the country could be uninhabitable; in 2021, 97% had already lost fresh groundwater.

title: Codasur South American Rally Championship
description: FIA-sanctioned rally championship run across South America since 1997, dominated by Paraguayan Gustavo Saba's six titles and a long Group N era before R5 cars took over.

title: Cody Ko
description: Cody Ko's YouTube channel — commentary, react videos, and comedy bits from the ex-software-engineer turned podcaster. Half of Tiny Meat Gang with Noel Miller.

title: Cody Tries — YouTube channel
description: Cody's YouTube channel built around model train layouts, builds, and railroad hobbyist content. Channel handle is @itscodytrains, the rest is URL-only inference.

title: ColdFusion
description: Dagogo Altraide's YouTube channel covering tech history, business stories, and the human side of innovation. Documentary-style explainers with a moody synth score he composes himself.

title: Colombian Coffee Growing Axis
description: Wikipedia on the Eje Cafetero — the Caldas/Risaralda/Quindío region where Colombia grew its primary export crop into a UNESCO Cultural Landscape. Manizales, Pereira, Armenia as the urban anchors.

title: color-name.com — color reference database
description: Database of named colors with hex codes, RGB values, and color theory metadata. The kind of site you land on when hunting down the exact shade of 'rebecca purple' or 'gamboge'.

title: Company Man
description: Mike's YouTube channel breaking down the rise and fall of American companies — Sears, Blockbuster, Toys R Us, regional fast food chains. Corporate history as quiet narrative video essays.

title: Confederados
description: Brazilian descendants of Confederate Southerners who fled Reconstruction for Emperor Dom Pedro II's slavery-tolerant Brazil, founding Americana in São Paulo. Up to 20,000 emigrated; their festival and Campo Cemetery still anchor the community.

title: Continuously Variable Transmission
description: Wikipedia on the CVT — the automatic transmission that sweeps through a continuous range of ratios instead of fixed gears. Covers pulley, toroidal, hydrostatic, and epicyclic designs across cars, scooters, and tractors.

title: CoolWorks — seasonal jobs in cool places
description: Job board for seasonal gigs at national parks, ranches, ski resorts, and summer camps. The place to find work flipping burgers in Yellowstone or wrangling at a dude ranch in Montana.

title: Cosmic microwave background
description: Wikipedia on the faint thermal afterglow of the Big Bang, discovered accidentally by Penzias and Wilson in 1965. Covers the COBE, WMAP, and Planck missions that turned it into precision cosmology.

title: Cost of Electricity by Country 2026 — World Population Review
description: Country-by-country ranking of residential electricity prices, with a 2026 data refresh. World Population Review's usual table-plus-commentary format on top of public utility data.

title: Countries by Traffic-Related Death Rate
description: Wikipedia's cross-country ranking of road fatalities — per capita, per vehicle, and per vehicle-km. WHO data pegs the global average at 17.4 deaths per 100,000, with low-income countries bearing more than double that.

title: Countries Where English Is an Official Language
description: Wikipedia's tally of the 58 sovereign states and 28 non-sovereign entities that designate English as official. Sorted by de jure, de facto, and predominant-but-undesignated status.

title: CoverageMap — crowdsourced cellular coverage maps
description: Cellular coverage maps built from millions of crowdsourced speed tests and signal measurements across four countries. Compare carriers side-by-side, plus an API and tile service for businesses.

title: Create More Than You Consume
description: Omar Itani's essay on how a daily dose of creative work — even 45 minutes — lowers cortisol and fills the void that endless scrolling leaves behind. Pandemic-era reflection.

title: Credit union
description: Wikipedia on member-owned nonprofit financial cooperatives — the not-a-bank that does most of what a bank does. Covers the global landscape, from SACCOs in Africa to billion-dollar US institutions.

title: Crisis de diciembre de 2001 en Argentina
description: Wikipedia en español on the December 2001 implosion — the corralito, the supermarket lootings, De la Rúa fleeing the Casa Rosada by helicopter, 39 dead. The week Argentina cycled through five presidents.

title: Cuevas — Argentina's Black-Market FX Explained
description: BowTiedMara walks through how Argentina's parallel dollar market actually operates: the blue rate, why it's roughly 2x the official rate, and how cuevas close deals over WhatsApp. Practical field guide from a Buenos Aires geoarbitrage writer.

title: CVS Caremark
description: Wikipedia on the pharmacy benefit management subsidiary of CVS Health. Started in 1993 as MedPartners, a Birmingham physician practice management shop, before pivoting to PBM and getting absorbed into the CVS empire.

title: Daihatsu
description: Wikipedia on Japan's oldest surviving car maker, now a Toyota subsidiary specializing in kei cars and small vehicles. Founded 1951 in Ikeda, Osaka; rocked by a 2023 safety-test rigging scandal.

title: Dalmatian language
description: Wikipedia on the extinct Romance language spoken along the Croatian coast until 1898, when its last fluent speaker Tuone Udaina died in a road-mining accident on Krk. Two main varieties documented: Ragusan and Vegliote.

title: DAREBEE — Home Workouts
description: Non-profit, ad-free fitness library with 2300+ no-equipment home workouts, monthly challenges, and multi-week programs. Donation-funded since 2012, new workouts dropped Monday through Thursday.

title: Darebee Ab Exercises Chart
description: Darebee's printable chart of ab exercises, laid out as an illustrated reference grid. Part of their free no-equipment fitness library.

title: Darling
description: Translation layer that runs macOS software on Linux, no hardware emulator. Wine for Darwin — implements Mach, dyld, launchd, and a Cocoa stack built on Cocotron and GNUstep.

title: DARPA's POWER program — wireless laser power record
description: New Atlas on DARPA's Persistent Optical Wireless Energy Relay program setting new records for power transmitted over distance via laser at White Sands. The pitch: laser beams instead of power lines for forward operations.

title: Dassler brothers feud
description: The Adi vs. Rudi Dassler split that birthed Adidas and Puma from one German shoe factory in Herzogenaurach. Includes the 1970 "Pelé Pact" Puma broke to sign him anyway.

title: December 2001 riots in Argentina
description: Wikipedia on the cacerolazo uprising that toppled Fernando de la Rúa, born from the corralito bank freeze and IMF-era collapse. Five presidents in eleven days.

title: Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area
description: Wikipedia on the EU's DCFTA agreements with Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine. Non-EEA states bolted into the Single Market through Association Agreements, with the Ukraine deal as the politically loaded one.

title: Defunct Automobile Manufacturers of the United States
description: Wikipedia's running A–Z roll call of dead American car companies, from Auburn Motor Chassis to forgotten one-model outfits like Abeln-Zehr. A century of automotive failure, sorted alphabetically.

title: Derinkuyu Underground City
description: Ancient multi-level city carved 85 meters into Cappadocian volcanic rock, sheltering up to 20,000 people with livestock and food stores. Phrygian-built in the 8th–7th century BC, later used by Byzantines and Cappadocian Greeks.

title: Devhints
description: Rico Sta. Cruz's sprawling collection of one-page cheatsheets — Bash, Vim, React, Sass, tmux, ffmpeg, you name it. The TL;DR layer over official docs that's been quietly maintained for years.

title: Diego Columbus — Lucayan adoptee
description: Wikipedia on the Lucayan Taíno boy abducted from Guanahani in 1492, baptized in Barcelona, and adopted by Christopher Columbus as his chief interpreter. Not the viceroy of the same name.

title: Digital nomad
description: Wikipedia on the wandering remote-worker lifestyle — laptops, cafés, mobile hotspots, and a growing list of countries issuing dedicated nomad visas. Tracks the post-2020 explosion from 7.5M to 18M+ American nomads.

title: DiploPlates countryList.txt — diplomatic plate country codes
description: The country code lookup table behind DiploPlates, a US diplomat license plate search tool. 1,075 lines mapping the cryptic two-letter codes on DPL tags to their issuing missions.

title: Discover Connection
description: YouTube channel exploring ways to bring connection back to modern life. Built around the premise that the most fulfilling life is one full of connection.

title: Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells
description: British shorthand for the reactionary letter-to-the-editor writer fuming from a stuffy Kent suburb. The phrase traces to a 1944 BBC radio show, a Times regular, or a local paper editor — no one's sure which.

title: Disk Prices
description: Live price-per-terabyte rankings for hard drives and SSDs scraped from Amazon. The shucking enthusiast's spreadsheet, sortable by $/TB, capacity, form factor, and warranty.

title: DisplaySpecifications
description: Spec database for desktop monitors and TVs, with side-by-side comparisons and a steady drip of new-panel news. The place to confirm whether that gaming monitor actually has 10-bit color.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
description: Wikipedia's full chronology of the USSR's unraveling from Gorbachev's 1985 election through the 1991 August coup and December collapse. Republic-by-republic, year-by-year.

title: Doctor of Credit
description: Long-running US credit card and bank account bonus tracker, run without affiliate links. The reference site for churning sign-up bonuses, direct-deposit tricks, and daily deal hunting.

title: Document — The Symbolism Survey
description: Paris Review blog post on Document, the project built around Bruce McAllister's 1963 high-school survey asking 150 famous novelists whether they intentionally planted symbols. Hemingway, Bellow, Kerouac, Updike all wrote back.

title: DocuSeal
description: Open-source document signing platform — the FOSS alternative to DocuSign and PandaDoc. Self-host it, or use the hosted version with API, embedded signing, and React components.

title: Dracaena cinnabari — Socotra dragon blood tree
description: Wikipedia on the umbrella-shaped dragon tree endemic to Socotra, named for the red resin it bleeds. Yemen's national tree, vulnerable on the IUCN list, and one of the weirder monocots — it does secondary growth like a dicot.

title: Drew Binsky
description: YouTube travel channel from Drew Binsky, who's been to every country on Earth. Short-form mini-docs on cultures, tribes, and weird border towns most travel vloggers skip.

title: Driving Right — Hong Kong's left-hand traffic
description: Zolima CityMag on whether Hong Kong will ever switch from left-hand to right-hand traffic, given mainland China drives on the right. A quirk-of-colonial-legacy explainer.

title: Drug policy of Portugal
description: Wikipedia on Portugal's 2001 decriminalization of personal drug possession. Originally a public-health response to HIV from injection use, routing users to Dissuasion Commissions instead of courts.

title: Dune of Pilat
description: The tallest sand dune in Europe, sitting at the mouth of Arcachon Bay southwest of Bordeaux. 106 meters high, 2.7 km long, and slowly marching inland over the forest and bits of the Atlantic Wall.

title: Earth Trekkers
description: Family travel blog from Julie, Tim, Tyler and Kara, who spent 13 months circling 35 countries and kept going. Heavy on US national parks, multi-week itineraries, and hiking guides.

title: Ease of Doing Business Index
description: Wikipedia on the World Bank's now-defunct ranking of national business regulations, founded in 2002 and killed in 2021 after two data-manipulation scandals.

title: East Germany's Coffee Crisis
description: Coffee or Die on the 1977 East German coffee crisis, when Honecker's regime ran out of hard currency to import beans and tried to push citizens onto ersatz blends. Cold War economics through the lens of a caffeine shortage.

title: Easy Languages
description: Berlin-based video and podcast network that teaches languages through unscripted street interviews. Spun out of Easy German into a global franchise of local co-producers.

title: Ecclesiastical Nagasaki
description: Wikipedia on the seven years Nagasaki was administered by the Jesuits under the Ōmura clan, 1580–1587. Not a Portuguese colony despite the common misreading — just commercial and religious privileges under the Padroado.

title: Economic history of Argentina
description: Wikipedia's full sweep of Argentina's economy from colonial silver to Milei's chainsaw. The country that went from one of the world's richest in 1913 to the textbook case for the 'Argentine paradox.'

title: Eighteen Stairs — Chongqing historic district
description: Wikipedia on the 400-meter stone staircase in Yuzhong, Chongqing — one of the city's five traditional-style districts, with over 200 steps connecting the upper and lower city. Reopened in stages from 2021 after a long renovation.

title: El Salvador's Gang Crackdown — NYT
description: New York Times dispatch on Bukele's mass-incarceration campaign against MS-13 and Barrio 18, reported from inside the state of exception that suspended civil liberties in 2022.

title: Embassy of Sweden, Pyongyang
description: Wikipedia on Sweden's embassy in North Korea, opened 1975 and long the only Western mission with uninterrupted presence there. Serves as the US protecting power and consular proxy for half a dozen other countries.

title: Empire of Brazil
description: Wikipedia on the 1822–1889 Brazilian monarchy under Pedro I and Pedro II — independence from Portugal through the Paraguayan War to the republican coup. Covers the slavery question that ultimately broke it.

title: Epicurious
description: Condé Nast's home-cooking site since 1995, with 33,000+ recipes plus technique guides and kitchen-gear reviews. The old-guard recipe archive before the food-blog era.

title: Erfurt latrine disaster
description: In 1184, sixty German nobles attending a court day with Henry VI crashed through a rotten wooden floor into the latrine cesspit below. Some drowned in human waste.

title: Erg Chebbi
description: Wikipedia on the erg in southeastern Morocco — 150-meter dunes spanning 28 km along the Algerian border, anchored by the tourist town of Merzouga.

title: Eternal September
description: The Usenet old guard's name for the moment in 1993 when AOL opened the floodgates and the yearly freshman influx never receded. Internet folklore's origin myth for every wave of newbies since.

title: Ethnic groups of Argentina
description: Wikipedia's survey of Argentina's ethnic makeup — the European waves (Italian, Spanish, German, Welsh), indigenous peoples (Mapuche, Guaraní, Diaguita), Afro-Argentines, and West Asian and East Asian communities.

title: Etruscan alphabet
description: Wikipedia on the script the Etruscans used from about 700 BC to 100 AD, adapted from the Euboean Greek alphabet at Pithekoussai and Cumae. Direct ancestor of the Latin alphabet.

title: Euphemisms for Internet censorship in China
description: Wikipedia on how Chinese netizens route around censorship with homophones — 'river crab' (héxiè) standing in for 'harmonize' after that word itself got censored. A small case study in linguistic cat-and-mouse.

title: European Kazakhstan
description: Wikipedia on the slice of Kazakhstan west of the Ural River — 148,000 km² that technically sits in Europe and makes Kazakhstan the continent's 14th-largest country, just edging out Greece.

title: EuroVelo — European long-distance cycle network
description: The European Cyclists' Federation's network of 17 long-distance cycle routes crossing the continent, from the Atlantic Coast to the Iron Curtain Trail. Route planner, GPX downloads, and country-by-country guides.

title: Exploiting the iPhone 4, Part 1: Gaining Entry
description: Phillip Tennen builds an iOS 4 jailbreak from scratch, starting with limera1n and DFU-mode code execution on the iPhone 4. First in a six-part reverse-engineering series.

title: Explore Vedado — Havana's "forbidden" neighborhood
description: insightCuba blog post on Vedado, the mid-century Havana district overshadowed by Old Havana. Tour-operator travel writing on the neighborhood's music, cafés, and Cold War-era architecture.

title: Fall of Kabul (2021)
description: Wikipedia's account of the Taliban's August 15, 2021 capture of Kabul — Ghani's flight, the airport evacuation, the Abbey Gate bombing, and the collapse of the twenty-year Afghan republic in a single day.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Wikipedia's long-form account of the West's unraveling from the Tetrarchy to Odoacer in 476. Covers Gibbon's thesis alongside contemporary climate, migration, and fiscal explanations.

title: Feds Ordered Google to Unmask YouTube Viewers
description: Forbes' Thomas Brewster on federal orders demanding Google identify everyone who watched specific YouTube videos. Privacy lawyers call the requests unconstitutional dragnets.

title: First Syrian Republic
description: Wikipedia on the Syrian state from 1930 to 1950 — French Mandate territory that became a sovereign republic in 1946, then fell to a military coup three years later.

title: FlyerTalk
description: The largest miles-and-points forum on the internet, running since 1998. Where status-chasers, mileage-runners, and award-booking obsessives swap intel on every airline and hotel program.

title: FMHY — freemediaheckyeah
description: The sprawling wiki-index of free stuff on the internet: streaming, downloading, piracy-adjacent tools, adblocking, AI, gaming. Reddit-born, mirrored everywhere, the canonical starting point.

title: Folklore.org — Original Macintosh stories
description: 123 firsthand anecdotes from the team that built the original Macintosh, collected by Andy Hertzfeld. The canonical oral history of the Mac, now archived by the Computer History Museum.

title: Fonts are still a Helvetica of a Problem
description: Canva security engineers find CVEs in font-processing tools by digging into the weird corners where SVG meets sfnt typography. Three vulnerabilities, three strange attack surfaces.

title: Food Waste by Country 2026 — World Population Review
description: World Population Review's country-by-country ranking of food waste, with per-capita and total figures. SEO-driven stats aggregator, sourced from UNEP and FAO data.

title: Ford CEO on China's EV Progress
description: Jim Farley tells Walter Isaacson at Aspen Ideas that China makes 70% of the world's EVs, with Huawei and Xiaomi tech baked in — and Ford has no future if it loses this race.

title: Fordlândia
description: Henry Ford's 1928 attempt to build a prefab American company town in the Amazon to secure rubber for his tires. Collapsed after worker revolts, leaf blight, and Ford never visiting.

title: Forget Monopoly — Chinatown Simulates Capitalism
description: FEE essay arguing Karsten Hartwig's 1999 board game Chinatown teaches market dynamics better than Monopoly. Trading-phase negotiation as a lesson in mutual gain.

title: Fort Ross, California
description: Wikipedia on the Russian-American Company's 1812 colonial outpost on the Sonoma coast — the southernmost reach of Russian North America before Mexico squeezed it out in 1841.

title: Fortifications of the Russian Invasion of Ukraine
description: Wikipedia survey of the trench networks, dragon's teeth, and bunker belts dug by both sides since 2022 — the Surovikin line, Wagner line, Zaluzhny line, and the rest. Trench warfare comparisons to WWI are doing real work here.

title: Founding of Rome
description: Wikipedia on how Rome actually came together — gradual union of hilltop villages in the 8th century BC — and the Romulus/Remus and Aeneas myths layered on top. Archaeology vs. legend, side by side.

title: France Automotive Loan Market Report — TechSci Research
description: TechSci Research's paywalled market report on France's auto loan sector, pegging it at USD 72.34 billion in 2024 with 5.67% CAGR through 2030. Standard industry-analyst boilerplate behind a sales wall.

title: Free drinking water — what are your rights?
description: BBC explainer on UK law around free tap water: licensed premises must provide it in England, Wales, and Scotland; gyms and cinemas don't have to; Northern Ireland mostly opts out.

title: Free Territory of Freedomland
description: The micronation Tomás Cloma declared over the Spratly Islands from 1956 to 1974, after his brother's fishing fleet got blown there by a typhoon and found the islands missing from every map.

title: Free Trade Area of the Americas
description: Wikipedia on the FTAA, the failed 2005 proposal to extend NAFTA across the hemisphere minus Cuba. Killed by the same North-South split that stalled the WTO's Doha round — ag subsidies versus IP rights.

title: Freedom to roam
description: Wikipedia on the public right to access private and public land for recreation — codified in the Nordics, Scotland, and a handful of others, ancient enough that most never bothered writing it down.

title: French colonial empire
description: Wikipedia's sweep of France's two colonial empires — the 16th-century Atlantic project that collapsed with Haiti and Napoleon, and the post-1830 push into Africa, Indochina, and the Pacific that unwound after WWII.

title: French Indochina
description: Wikipedia on the French colonial federation in Southeast Asia (1887–1954), spanning Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia. Ends with Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Agreements that set up the American war.

title: French Petitions Against Age-of-Consent Laws
description: Wikipedia on the 1977 and 1979 petitions, signed by Foucault, Sartre, Beauvoir and other French intellectuals, urging the abolition of France's age-of-consent laws. A grim artifact of late-70s Parisian intellectual culture.

title: French Resistance
description: Wikipedia on the rebel networks that fought Nazi occupation in France from 1940 to 1944. Covers the Gaullists, communists, maquis, Jean Moulin's unification effort, and the messy post-liberation purges.

title: Gagauzia
description: Wikipedia on the Turkic-speaking autonomous region in southern Moldova, capital Comrat. Christian Orthodox Gagauz declared independence in 1990 before settling for autonomy in 1995.

title: Galton–Watson process
description: Wikipedia on the branching stochastic process Francis Galton devised in 1869 to model the extinction of aristocratic surnames. Now load-bearing across population genetics, nuclear fission, and probability theory.

title: Game Theory 101
description: William Spaniel's YouTube channel teaching game theory from Nash equilibria to nuclear deterrence. The companion to his textbook series — short, whiteboard-style lectures aimed at undergrads.

title: Gamma — AI presentation and deck builder
description: AI-native tool for generating presentations, documents, and webpages from a prompt. Pitched as a faster alternative to PowerPoint and Google Slides, with auto-layout and brand theming.

title: GCHQ
description: The UK's signals intelligence agency, headquartered in the Cheltenham 'Doughnut.' Founded 1919 as the Government Code and Cypher School — the Bletchley Park outfit that broke Enigma before it got its current name in 1946.

title: Geo Companion — geography web app
description: Vercel-hosted geography companion app. Thin landing page with no description; the name is the only signal about what it does.

title: Geographical distribution of French speakers
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country breakdown of where French is spoken — from the Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa to Quebec, Haiti, Lebanon, and the Channel Islands. Tracks how French became Europe's diplomatic lingua franca before the colonial spread.

title: GeoGrid — geography guessing game
description: Daily geography puzzle in a 3x3 grid. Fill each cell with a country matching the row and column criteria, Immaculate Grid style applied to world geography.

title: GeoGuessr
description: Geography game that drops you into a Street View panorama and asks you to pin your location on a world map. Spawned a whole competitive scene with tournaments and a World Championship.

title: Geoguessr Explained
description: YouTube channel teaching how to get closer guesses in Geoguessr through meta-knowledge and regional clues. Collaborative tone over competitive — tips for new and experienced players alike.

title: GeoHints
description: Reference site for GeoGuessr players cataloging country-identifying meta-clues — bollards, license plates, utility poles, road lines, follow cars, sign backs. Organized by category, drillable down to specific countries.

title: German reunification
description: Wikipedia on the 1989–1991 absorption of East Germany into the Federal Republic. Covers the economic merger, the Two Plus Four Treaty, the Polish border settlement, and the lingering Ossi-Wessi cost ledger.

title: Ghost Dance
description: Wikipedia on the 1889–1891 Native American religious movement founded by Northern Paiute prophet Wovoka. Promised the dead would return and westward expansion would end — culminated at Wounded Knee.

title: Giacomo Casanova
description: Wikipedia on the 18th-century Venetian adventurer whose posthumous memoir Histoire de ma vie became the defining first-person record of Enlightenment Europe's libertine underworld. Died a librarian in Bohemia.

title: Giant's Causeway
description: Wikipedia on the 40,000 interlocking basalt columns on the Antrim coast, formed by a Paleogene fissure eruption. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986, and the setting for the Finn McCool legend.

title: Glagolitic script
description: Wikipedia on the oldest known Slavic alphabet, devised by Saint Cyril around 862 to render Old Church Slavonic. Survived in Croatian liturgical use into the 19th century, long after Cyrillic displaced it elsewhere.

title: Glittering generality
description: Wikipedia on the propaganda technique of emotionally loaded phrases — freedom, honor, equality — that win assent without argument. Traces the term to Rufus Choate's 1851 swipe at abolitionist rhetoric.

title: Global city
description: Wikipedia on the concept of cities that anchor the global economy — New York and London at the top, then the GaWC Alpha+ tier. Covers the major ranking systems (GaWC, Kearney, Oxford Economics, GPCI).

title: Golden Age of Piracy
description: Wikipedia on maritime piracy from the 1650s to the 1730s, split into the buccaneering period, the Pirate Round, and the post-Spanish Succession era. Blackbeard, Tortuga, Madagascar bases, and the Caribbean-to-Indian-Ocean arc.

title: Good Work Cafes
description: Crowdsourced directory of cafes worth working from, rated on wifi, outlets, noise, and seating. Remote-worker scouting tool, city by city.

title: Goodpods
description: Social podcast app built around what your friends and tastemakers are actually listening to. Charts, shared playlists, and follow-based discovery instead of algorithmic guesswork.

title: Google Labs
description: Google's public-facing showcase for its AI experiments — Flow, Stitch, Pomelli, Illuminate, and a rotating cast of research prototypes you can sign up to try. The front door for stuff that hasn't graduated into a real product yet.

title: Google redraws disputed borders depending on who's looking
description: Greg Bensinger's 2020 Washington Post piece on how Google Maps quietly redraws Kashmir, Crimea, and the Korean DMZ based on the viewer's country. Cartography as soft diplomacy.

title: Google's true origin partly lies in CIA and NSA research grants
description: Quartz piece tracing Google's founding back to mid-90s CIA and NSA funding for mass-surveillance research at Stanford. The intelligence-community-as-incubator angle on Silicon Valley.

title: Government Reform of Peter the Great
description: Wikipedia on how Peter I rebuilt Russian government on Western European lines between 1696 and 1725 — Senate, Collegia, Table of Ranks, and a tax system bent around funding the Great Northern War.

title: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
description: Wikipedia on the 145-meter gravity dam on the Blue Nile, operational since 2020 and the flashpoint of a long-running water-rights fight between Ethiopia, Sudan, and Egypt.

title: Green Ukraine
description: Wikipedia on Zelenyi Klyn, the Ukrainian name for the Russian Far East between the Amur and the Pacific. Ukrainian settlers moved east during Imperial expansion; after 1917 they briefly tried to secede as an ethnostate.

title: Griffin / Wordsatwork
description: Griffin's YouTube channel on languages and their idiosyncrasies, plus music, Chicago, and Toki Pona — sometimes all at once. This is the shorts feed.

title: groups-for-nomads
description: Crowdsourced directory of Telegram, WhatsApp, and Facebook groups for travelers and digital nomads, organized by city and country. Community-maintained on GitHub with 83 stars and steady PR traffic.

title: GSMArena
description: The reference site for mobile phone specs, reviews, and news. Exhaustive database covering basically every handset ever shipped, plus daily industry coverage.

title: GUAM Organization for Democracy and Economic Development
description: Wikipedia on the post-Soviet regional bloc of Georgia, Ukraine, Azerbaijan, and Moldova — a Russia-skeptic alternative to the CIS founded in 1997, headquartered in Kyiv.

title: Guaraná
description: Wikipedia on the Amazonian climbing plant whose seeds run up to 6% caffeine — double a coffee bean. The reason Brazilian soft drinks hit the way they do.

title: Guarani language
description: Wikipedia on Paraguayan Guarani, the Tupian language co-official with Spanish in Paraguay and spoken natively by 6.5 million. One of the few Indigenous American languages that became a national majority tongue.

title: Gulf Pidgin Arabic
description: Wikipedia on the Arabic-based pidgin spoken by South and Southeast Asian migrant workers in the Persian Gulf. Stuck as a pidgin because workers never naturalize, marry in, or pass it to children.

title: Gypsy Lore Society
description: British scholarly society founded 1888 to study Romani history, language, and culture. Charles Leland was its first president; it's been headquartered in the US since 1989 and still publishes the journal Romani Studies.

title: h0ser
description: YouTube channel from h0ser. Content focus isn't visible from the URL alone — handle suggests hacking, hosting, or gaming-adjacent territory.

title: Half as Interesting
description: Sam Denby's spinoff from Wendover Productions — shorter, sillier explainers on aviation oddities, geopolitical loopholes, and trivia too thin to carry a full Wendover episode.

title: Hallstatt
description: Tiny lakeside village in Upper Austria wedged between the Hallstätter See and the Dachstein massif. Lent its name to the Hallstatt culture of the early Iron Age, and now drowns in day-tripper overtourism — there's a full-scale replica of it in China.

title: Hanlon's razor
description: The adage "never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity." Named for a Robert J. Hanlon who submitted it to a 1980 Murphy's Law joke book, with an earlier Heinlein variant from 1941.

title: Harlem Renaissance
description: Wikipedia on the 1918–mid-1930s African-American cultural movement centered in Harlem. Literature, jazz, painting, theater, and the New Negro identity that fed into everything that came after.

title: Harris briefly acting president during Biden's colonoscopy
description: Reuters dispatch on the 85-minute power transfer to Kamala Harris on November 19, 2021 — the first time a woman held presidential authority in U.S. history, however technically.

title: Hatay Province
description: Turkey's southernmost province, capital Antakya (ancient Antioch), wedged against the Syrian border. Disputed territory until 1939, devastated by the 2023 earthquakes, and home to a mixed Turkish-Arab-Alawite population.

title: Hatay State
description: Wikipedia on the short-lived Turkish-French puppet republic that existed for ten months in 1938–39 before being absorbed into Turkey. The mechanism by which France handed Alexandretta to Ankara on the eve of WWII.

title: Healthy Recipes Blog
description: Vered DeLeeuw's recipe site, running since 2011, focused on real-food, low-carb, gluten-free cooking. Every recipe is reviewed by a registered dietitian.

title: Helix
description: Post-modern modal text editor in Rust, built around Kakoune-style multi-selection and tree-sitter. Terminal-only, no plugins yet, language servers work out of the box.

title: HelloTalk
description: Language exchange app pairing you with native speakers for chat, voice, and video. Claims 70M+ users across 260+ languages, with built-in translation and correction tools.

title: Hi Clavero — YouTube channel
description: YouTube channel of Hi Clavero. Page is a JS shell so the channel's actual subject can't be confirmed from the URL alone.

title: Hippolyte Bouchard
description: French-born corsair who fought for Argentina in the Spanish American wars of independence, raided Spanish California in 1818, and briefly held Monterey under the Argentine flag. Known locally as Pirata Buchar.

title: History of Hadrian's Wall
description: English Heritage's overview of Hadrian's Wall, the Roman empire's north-west frontier for nearly 300 years. Construction began in AD 122 under Hadrian; now a World Heritage Site.

title: History of Tajikistan
description: Wikipedia's sweep through Tajik history from the Achaemenids to independence — Sassanids, Samanids, Timurids, Basmachi revolt, Soviet ASSR, 1991. The Ismail Samani statue in Dushanbe is the through-line.

title: holdall — remote-work destination guide
description: Solo-traveler trip reports from a Deel product-team remote worker hopping cities month by month. Numeric scorecards, café notes, and blunt verdicts like "little to love about Casablanca."

title: Holden
description: Wikipedia on the defunct Australian automaker, founded as a saddlery in Adelaide in 1856 and shuttered by GM in 2021 after 164 years. The marque that defined Australian car culture.

title: Holy Right Hand of St. Stephen — Atlas Obscura
description: The mummified right hand of Hungary's first king, venerated for a thousand years and paraded through Budapest every August 20th. Now enshrined in St. Stephen's Basilica.

title: Hoover free flights promotion
description: In 1992 Hoover UK offered two round-trip US flights to anyone spending £100 on appliances, betting customers wouldn't bite. They did — the fiasco cost the royal warrant and sank the European arm into Candy's hands.

title: Hot mess as 23 relatives crash on blind date
description: The Star reports on a Zhejiang blind date that turned legal after the woman showed up with 23 relatives in tow. Brief wire-style oddity item.

title: Housing First
description: Wikipedia on the homelessness policy that gives people permanent housing first, then wraps services around them — no sobriety or treatment preconditions. Country-by-country evidence sections from Finland to the U.S.

title: How Big Is America's Underground Economy?
description: Investopedia explainer on the scale of U.S. off-the-books activity — cash work, unreported income, illicit markets — and how economists try to size something nobody reports.

title: How Havana Is Collapsing, Building by Building
description: USA Today dispatch on Havana's housing crisis — 3,856 building collapses from 2000–2013, 28,000 people in structures that could fall any moment, even as UNESCO-listed Old Havana wins restoration awards.

title: How Intel lost mobile to Apple's Ax chips
description: Daniel Eran Dilger's 2015 AppleInsider postmortem on Intel fumbling mobile between 2005 and 2014 while Apple's A-series ARM chips ate the market. Twelve minutes of partisan but detailed industry history.

title: How Kazakhstan Helps Russia Bypass Western Sanctions
description: The Diplomat on the parallel-imports pipeline routing Western goods through Kazakhstan into sanctioned Russia. Untangles how the EAEU customs union, ruble-tenge convertibility, and local corruption make enforcement structurally impossible.

title: How the US 'totally destroyed' North Korea
description: David McNeill in the Irish Times on the 1950-53 US bombing campaign that flattened North Korean cities — half a million tons of bombs, napalm, chemical weapons. The forgotten context behind Pyongyang's hostility.

title: How to Delete Your Data From Data Brokers — Cyber Collective
description: Cyber Collective's walkthrough on opting out of Acxiom, Experian, Equifax, and the rest. Covers access requests, removal letters, and the consumer protection laws that back them.

title: How to tie a secure shoelace knot — Ian's Shoelace Site
description: Ian Fieggen's fix for shoelaces that won't stay tied: a double-wrap on the first half of the bow. Part of the obsessive shoelace compendium that's been online since the 90s.

title: How Waze Beacons Work
description: Waze's spec for the BLE micro-controllers it installs in tunnels to keep routing alive where GPS dies. Eddystone UID/TLM packets, 4-6 year battery, free for other nav apps to use.

title: Huemul Project
description: Argentina's 1951 attempt at fusion power, run by Austrian scientist Ronald Richter on an island near Bariloche under Perón's patronage. Pure fraud, but it kicked off serious fusion research worldwide.

title: Hyperpalatable food
description: Wikipedia on foods engineered to hijack the brain's reward system through specific fat/sugar/salt/carb thresholds. The University of Kansas criteria pinned 69% of US food sales as hyperpalatable by 2018.

title: Hyrcanian forests
description: Ancient temperate broadleaf forest belt hugging the Caspian's southern shore across Iran and Azerbaijan. A 55,000-square-kilometre Pleistocene refugium, UNESCO-listed since 2019.

title: IAEA Board of Governors Report GOV/2025/24
description: IAEA Board of Governors document from June 2025. Official agency report — almost certainly the safeguards verification update on Iran's nuclear program that triggered the censure resolution that month.

title: Ibadism
description: Wikipedia on Ibadism, the third-largest branch of Islam — older than Sunni or Shia, founded c. 692 in Basra, and now concentrated in Oman, Zanzibar, and pockets of the Maghreb.

title: ibx2cat — YouTube channel
description: YouTube channel of ibx2cat, a hacker known for iOS jailbreak work and low-level exploit research. Sporadic uploads covering reverse engineering and security tinkering.

title: Ice — macOS menu bar manager
description: Open-source macOS menu bar manager by Jordan Baird. Hides and rearranges menu bar items, with drag-and-drop ordering, item search, and custom spacing.

title: Idiolect
description: Wikipedia on the linguistic concept of an individual's unique use of language — vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation. Distinct from dialect, which is shared across a group, and load-bearing in forensic linguistics for authorship attribution.

title: Igor Smirnov
description: Wikipedia on the first president of Transnistria, who ran the unrecognized breakaway republic from 1991 to 2011. Russian-born factory manager turned separatist strongman in the Moldova-Ukraine borderlands.

title: Illegal border crossings overwhelm New York towns — Adirondack Explorer
description: Times Union report, republished by Adirondack Explorer, on the surge of migrants crossing illegally from Canada into northern New York and the strain on small Adirondack-region towns.

title: Independence of Brazil
description: Wikipedia on Brazil's 1822 break from Portugal, centered on Pedro I's Cry of Ipiranga and the war that followed across Pernambuco, Bahia, and Cisplatina.

title: Independent State of Croatia
description: Wikipedia on the Nezavisna Država Hrvatska, the 1941–1945 Axis puppet state run by the Ustaše. Covers the regime's genocide policies, Italian and German zones of influence, and Partisan resistance through the war's end.

title: India's Hindus Bathe In Holy River Defiled By Pollution
description: AFP dispatch on thousands of Hindu devotees wading into the sewage-choked Yamuna in Delhi, defying court warnings against bathing in the toxic foam. A snapshot of India's capital drowning in its own waste.

title: Indian Packing Company
description: Wikipedia on the defunct Delaware canned-meat outfit that bankrolled Curly Lambeau's Green Bay team in 1919. The Packers kept the name; the company was gone by 1921.

title: Instrument for Pre-accession Assistance (IPA)
description: The EU's funding mechanism for prepping enlargement candidates — Western Balkans plus Türkiye — for membership. IPA III runs 2021–2027 with a €14.16 billion envelope.

title: Insult and Passphrase Generator
description: Ron Hardin's algorithmic insult generator, served plain on Bill Cheswick's site. Each refresh yields a fresh Shakespearean-flavored slur like "You dreary vial of miasmal humpback squirt."

title: International Status and Usage of the Euro
description: Wikipedia on how the euro travels beyond the eurozone — from Andorra and Monaco's mint deals to unilateral adopters like Montenegro, plus its slow climb as a reserve currency rival to the dollar.

title: International use of the U.S. dollar
description: Wikipedia on how the dollar became and stayed the world's reserve currency — Bretton Woods, dollarization, eurodollar deposits, and the 75% of $100 bills held overseas.

title: Interstate Highway System
description: Wikipedia on the 48,890-mile US freeway network Eisenhower signed into law in 1956. Covers the numbering scheme, financing via fuel taxes, and the urban neighborhoods it bulldozed along the way.

title: Islamic Golden Age
description: Wikipedia's overview of the 8th–14th century period when Baghdad, Cairo, and Córdoba ran the intellectual frontier — algebra, optics, medicine, translation of the Greek corpus. Runs from 786 to the Mongol sack of Baghdad in 1258.

title: Itaipu Dam
description: Wikipedia on the Brazil–Paraguay hydroelectric dam on the Paraná River, opened 1984 at a cost of $19.6 billion. One of the Seven Wonders of the Modern World, jointly owned by both governments.

title: Italian Brazilians
description: Wikipedia on the Italian diaspora in Brazil — roughly 32 million descendants, mostly in the South and Southeast, plus the Talian dialect that survives in Rio Grande do Sul.

title: italki
description: Marketplace for 1-on-1 language lessons with 20,000+ tutors across 150+ languages. No subscription — book teachers à la carte, pay per lesson, schedule on your own clock.

title: Itchy Boots
description: Noraly Schoenmaker solo-rides a Royal Enfield Himalayan across the world's remote backroads — Pamir, Patagonia, Africa. Long-form adventure motorcycle vlogging at scale.

title: JackSucksAtGeography
description: YouTube channel from Jack Massey Welsh spun off from JackSucksAtLife, dedicated to geography quizzes, country rankings, and flag trivia. Entertaining first, occasionally educational.

title: Jangmadang
description: Wikipedia on North Korea's informal markets, born from the 1990s famine and now load-bearing for survival. Also where you learn how black-market trade quietly shifted gender roles in the DPRK.

title: Japanese Occupation of Malaya
description: Wikipedia on the 1941–1945 Japanese military occupation of British Malaya, from the Kota Bharu landing through the Pacific War, Thai annexation of four northern states, and the postwar British return.

title: Jarvis Johnson
description: YouTube channel of Jarvis Johnson, ex-software engineer turned commentary creator. Long video essays on internet drama, reality TV, and creator culture, delivered deadpan.

title: JCDecaux
description: French outdoor advertising giant founded by Jean-Claude Decaux in 1964, now the world's largest in its sector with ads on 140,000 bus stops and 145 airports. Also the company behind Vélib-style bike-share systems.

title: Jeff Geerling
description: Personal site of the YouTuber, author, and maker known for Raspberry Pi deep-dives, homelab tinkering, and hardware reverse-engineering. Blog posts cover everything from patching iozone on Apple Silicon to FM radio on a 3D printer heatbed.

title: Jeff Geerling
description: YouTube channel from the Ansible for DevOps author covering Raspberry Pi, homelab tinkering, and self-hosted infrastructure. Heavy on Pi cluster builds and ARM hardware reviews.

title: Jeff Nippard
description: YouTube channel from the Canadian natural bodybuilder and biochem grad — evidence-based hypertrophy and strength training videos that actually cite the studies. One of the few fitness channels worth trusting.

title: Jet Lag: The Game
description: YouTube channel from Wendover Productions where hosts play elaborate competitive games across real-world geography — hide-and-seek across Europe, tag across Japan, races spanning continents.

title: Jining–Tongliao railway
description: Wikipedia on the 923-km Inner Mongolia line that opened in 1995 with deliberately anachronistic tech — semaphores, manned crossings, steam — and ran the world's last mainline steam service.

title: João Micaelo — Kim Jong-un's Portuguese best friend
description: Contacto profile of João Micaelo, the Portuguese classmate who befriended Kim Jong-un during the future North Korean leader's anonymous school years in Switzerland.

title: John Deere World Headquarters — Docomomo register entry
description: Docomomo's register page for Eero Saarinen's last major commission, the rural Deere & Company campus in Moline, Illinois. Gold-tinted mirrored glass, exposed Cor-Ten steel, brise-soleil, bridges over a lake.

title: John Paul Jones
description: Scottish-born naval officer who fought for the Continental Navy in the Revolutionary War, then served as a rear admiral under Catherine the Great. The 'Father of the American Navy', buried at Annapolis.

title: Johnny Harris
description: YouTube channel from the ex-Vox video journalist behind Borders. Explainer documentaries on geopolitics, maps, and why countries behave the way they do, with a heavy investigative bent.

title: Josef Albers
description: German-American painter and Bauhaus émigré whose Homage to the Square series turned color theory into a life's work. Taught at Black Mountain College and Yale, shaping a generation of postwar American artists.

title: Kafala system
description: Wikipedia on the Gulf and Levant sponsorship system that ties migrant workers' residency and employment to a single employer. The legal scaffolding behind the World Cup labor abuses and Lebanon's domestic-worker crisis.

title: KaiOS
description: Mobile OS for feature phones, forked from the discontinued Firefox OS / Boot to Gecko project. Runs JavaScript apps on cheap hardware — the software behind JioPhone and the late-2010s feature-phone revival in India and Africa.

title: Kamienica "Pekin" — Warsaw tenement reborn
description: Onet travel piece on the century-old "Pekin" tenement in central Warsaw, renovated after years of decay into 146 long-term rental flats ranging 26–116 m².

title: Karbovanets
description: Wikipedia on Ukraine's pre-hryvnia currency, issued in four separate runs across the 20th century — Central Rada, Hetmanate, Nazi occupation, and post-Soviet hyperinflation coupon.

title: Karelian question
description: Wikipedia on the Finnish political dispute over whether to reclaim the Karelia territory ceded to the Soviet Union in the 1940 Moscow Peace Treaty. Also covers Petsamo, Salla, and Kuusamo.

title: Karl Bushby
description: English ex-paratrooper attempting the first unbroken walk around the world. Started in Chile in 1998 as the Goliath Expedition; projected to finish in England in late 2026.

title: Karl Bushby & The Goliath Expedition
description: Profile of the British ex-paratrooper attempting the first unbroken walk around the world — 58,000 km from Punta Arenas to Hull, on foot since 1998, including a Bering Strait ice crossing.

title: Katpana Desert
description: Wikipedia on the high-altitude cold desert in Skardu Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan — sand dunes at 2,226m that get buried in snow each winter. One of the highest deserts on earth.

title: Katyn massacre
description: Wikipedia on the 1940 Soviet execution of roughly 22,000 Polish officers, intelligentsia, and POWs in Katyn Forest and nearby prisons. Stalin signed the order; the USSR blamed Germany until 1990.

title: Kei truck
description: Wikipedia on Japan's keijidōsha-class mini pickups — sub-660cc, under 3.4m long, built since 1959. Now a cult import in North America for being cheap, reliable, and weirdly charming.

title: Khrushchevka
description: Wikipedia on the cheap concrete-panel apartment blocks Khrushchev mass-produced across the USSR from 1956 to the mid-1970s. Four to five stories, functionalist, built fast to end the postwar housing crisis — and still standing everywhere from Tomsk to Gatchina.

title: Kim Jong-un's missile-shaped skyscrapers have one major design flaw
