description: Metro tabloid piece on Pyongyang's new Hwasong-district towers, shaped like missiles, where the lifts only run during the three-hour evening window when the grid has power.

title: Kingdom of Ireland
description: Wikipedia on the Irish kingdom that ran from 1542 to 1800 as a dependency first of England, then Great Britain. Covers the Tudor conquest, Stuart upheavals, Grattan's Patriots, and the United Irishmen up to the Act of Union.

title: Kintsugi
description: Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold, silver, or platinum lacquer. Treats the breakage as part of the object's history rather than something to hide — tied to the tea ceremony since the 15th century.

title: Kopi luwak
description: Indonesian coffee made from cherries eaten and defecated by Asian palm civets, then collected from the forest floor. Famous for its price, infamous for the caged-civet industry that now supplies most of it.

title: Kremlin-occupied Ukraine is now a totalitarian hell
description: The Economist on life inside Russian-occupied Ukraine — surveillance, forced passportization, disappearances. Reported dispatch from November 2024, two and a half years into the full-scale war.

title: KRL-D — North Korea's official site in Poland
description: The DPRK's Polish-language embassy portal in Warsaw: bulletins, Pyongyang Times issues, Juche ideology texts, and visa forms. A working artifact of North Korean diplomatic propaganda, in Polish.

title: Kurdistan
description: Wikipedia on the stateless Kurdish region straddling Turkey, Iraq, Iran, and Syria. Covers the etymology, the carve-up after the Ottoman collapse, and the modern autonomous zones in Erbil and Rojava.

title: Kurds
description: Wikipedia's overview of the Kurdish people — Iranic ethnic group spread across Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Syria, with deep dives into language, religion, nationalism, and the stateless politics of Kurdistan.

title: Kyrgyzstan Mountain Ranges and Peaks
description: Advantour's overview of Kyrgyzstan's 88+ mountain ranges, dominated by the Tian Shan with a slice of the Pamirs in the south. Useful primer on the Snow Leopard peaks and the north-south divide that shapes the country.

title: Lake Baikal
description: Wikipedia on the deepest and oldest lake on Earth — a 25-million-year-old rift lake in southern Siberia holding roughly a fifth of the planet's unfrozen freshwater. Endemic wildlife includes the nerpa, the only exclusively freshwater seal.

title: Lake Nyos disaster
description: In 1986 a limnic eruption at a crater lake in northwestern Cameroon released a 300,000-ton CO2 cloud that suffocated 1,746 people and 3,500 livestock within 25 km. One of only two recorded limnic eruptions in history.

title: Lake Victoria
description: Wikipedia on Africa's largest lake by area, shared by Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya. Source of the White Nile, home to the cichlid radiation that Nile perch introduction nearly wiped out.

title: LAN Party House
description: Kenton Varda and Jade Wang built a house in Austin with 20 netbooted gaming PCs in the walls, DDR pads in the floor, and cat catwalks throughout. Tour and Q&A from the Cloudflare Workers tech lead.

title: Language Tools Directory
description: Hand-curated directory of language-learning tools, sliced by language, pricing, and tags like #srs, #tutors, or #podcast. Covers 100+ languages including the long tail — Quechua, Sylheti, Tuvan, Navajo.

title: Languages of Belize
description: Wikipedia on Belize's language mix — English official, Spanish and Kriol both past 40%, plus Q'eqchi', Mopan, Yucatec Maya, Garifuna, and Plautdietsch German. 2022 census breakdown by district included.

title: Languages of Europe
description: Wikipedia's overview of the 250+ languages indigenous to Europe, dominated by the Indo-European family — Romance, Germanic, and Slavic together cover ~90% of speakers. Includes Uralic, Turkic, Semitic, and sign-language outliers.

title: LaSuite — French government work suite
description: France's open-source, sovereign workspace for public servants, bundling chat (Tchap), video (Visio), docs, files, and a Grist-based spreadsheet. Built by DINUM, used monthly by 500,000+ agents across 15 ministries.

title: Lateral with Tom Scott
description: Tom Scott's comedy panel game podcast built around lateral-thinking puzzles — weird questions with wonderful answers, posed to rotating guests each week.

title: Lava Lamp Encryption — Cloudflare's wall of lamps
description: Cloudflare's explainer on the LavaRand wall at their San Francisco HQ — a hundred lava lamps filmed to seed cryptographic randomness. The famous party trick of internet infrastructure.

title: Law French
description: Wikipedia on the Anglo-Norman dialect that ran English courts from the 13th to 18th centuries. Source of half the opaque vocabulary still floating around common law — voir dire, oyez, cestui que.

title: Lebanon
description: Wikipedia's country article on Lebanon — Mediterranean nation with a deep Phoenician past, sectarian power-sharing politics, and the 2019-present economic collapse that gutted the lira.

title: Lee Kuan Yew
description: Wikipedia on Singapore's founding prime minister, who ran the city-state from 1959 to 1990 and engineered its transformation from colonial port to high-income technocracy. Also the architect of the soft-authoritarian playbook everyone still argues about.

title: Leica Camera
description: Wikipedia on the German optics firm founded by Ernst Leitz in Wetzlar in 1869. The name is a portmanteau — Leitz + camera — and the company more or less invented 35mm photography.

title: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park — CNN Travel
description: CNN Travel dispatch on Brazil's 598-square-mile dunescape in Maranhão, where cerulean rain-fed lagoons pool between the white sand ridges from March to September.

title: Letters of Last Resort
description: Four handwritten letters from the UK prime minister to the commanders of Britain's Vanguard-class submarines, telling them what to do if the government and its designated successors are wiped out by a nuclear strike. Destroyed unopened when the PM leaves office.

title: Level2Jeff
description: Jeff's second YouTube channel for ServeTheHome — homelab, server hardware, and enterprise networking gear in a looser, vlog-style format. The off-the-cuff counterpart to the main STH channel.

title: Li Kwoh-ting
description: Wikipedia on the Taiwanese economist and KMT minister called the Father of Taiwan's Economic Miracle. Forty years of policy work that turned an agrarian island into a semiconductor powerhouse.

title: Lidl
description: German discount supermarket chain that's Aldi's chief rival across Europe and beyond. Founded 1930 by Josef Schwarz in Heilbronn, now part of the Schwarz Group with 12,200 stores and €132B revenue.

title: Lima — Linux VMs on macOS
description: Launches Linux virtual machines with automatic file sharing and port forwarding, WSL2-style, on macOS and beyond. CNCF incubating project, originally built to run containerd without Docker Desktop.

title: Lingthusiasm
description: Monthly podcast where linguists Gretchen McCulloch and Lauren Gawne geek out about hidden patterns in everyday language — proxemics, palatalization, singular they, the works.

title: Liquid Death's Wild Ride — Inc. Magazine
description: Inc.'s 2022 profile of Liquid Death, the heavy-metal-branded canned water startup that turned a joke premise into a nine-figure DTC brand. Alex Bhattacharji on the marketing playbook.

title: Lissachatina fulica — giant African land snail
description: Wikipedia on the giant African land snail, a federally prohibited invasive species in the US and the most widespread invasive snail worldwide. Also a rat lungworm vector.

title: List of Argentine Provinces by HDI
description: Argentina's 23 provinces and CABA ranked by Human Development Index, 2021 data from the UNDP. Buenos Aires City leads at 0.882; Chaco trails at 0.808.

title: List of Countries by English-Speaking Population
description: Wikipedia table ranking countries by native and second-language English speakers. Flagged for outdated sources and disputed accuracy since 2022, so treat the numbers as ballpark.

title: List of Countries by Ethnic Groups
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country breakdown of ethnic composition, pulled mostly from CIA World Factbook and national censuses. The article itself warns the categories aren't comparable across borders.

title: List of Countries by Human Development Index
description: Wikipedia's ranking of every country by HDI — life expectancy, education, and income rolled into one number. Based on 2023 data published by UNDP in 2025.

title: List of countries by obesity rate
description: Wikipedia's ranking of 191 countries by adult obesity prevalence, using WHO 2022 data. Tonga, Nauru, and Tuvalu top the table at 70%+; the US sits at 13th.

title: List of countries by suicide rate
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country ranking of age-standardized suicide rates per 100,000, with WHO data and a map shaded by band. Includes the small-population distortion caveat up top.

title: List of Countries with Overseas Military Bases
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country rundown of who keeps military installations abroad. The US section dwarfs everything else, but Turkey, Russia, France, India, and the UK all show up with real footprints.

title: List of Diplomatic Missions of North Korea
description: Wikipedia's running roster of every DPRK embassy, consulate, and UN mission still open — plus the ones it's quietly shuttered. A map of who Pyongyang still talks to.

title: List of Freedom Indices
description: Wikipedia's roundup of the major freedom rankings — Freedom House, Human Freedom Index, Economic Freedom of the World, V-Dem — with what each measures and who publishes it. Handy when you need to know which index says what.

title: List of Highest-Grossing Concert Tours
description: Wikipedia's running ledger of the biggest touring paydays in history, sourced from Billboard and Pollstar boxscores. Taylor Swift's Eras Tour sits on top at $2.07 billion — the first to clear two.

title: List of Indian Reservations in the United States
description: Wikipedia's master table of the ~567 federally recognized reservations, plus trust lands, Alaska Native village areas, Hawaiian home lands, and state-recognized territories. Population, acreage, and tribe for each.

title: List of Lakes by Area
description: Wikipedia's ranked list of the world's largest lakes above 3,000 km², split into a conventional list and a geological one that treats the Caspian as an ocean fragment and merges Michigan–Huron into a single body.

title: List of metro systems
description: Wikipedia's running tally of every electrified rapid-transit system on Earth — 214 cities, 63 countries, 950 lines as of 2026. Sortable by length, ridership, opening date, and country.

title: List of Most Expensive TV Series
description: Wikipedia's running tally of TV production budgets per episode. Rings of Power season 1 leads at $58M/episode; Marvel's Disney+ slate clusters around $25M apiece.

title: List of Placeholder Names
description: Wikipedia's catalog of placeholder names across thirty-odd languages — the foreign-language equivalents of John Doe, Joe Bloggs, and whatchamacallit. Organized by language, then by persons, places, and things.

title: List of Popes
description: Wikipedia's chronological roster of every pope from Peter to the present, following the Annuario Pontificio and excluding antipopes. Notes that the Vatican itself has stopped assigning regnal numbers because the legitimate succession can't always be settled.

title: List of Roman emperors
description: Wikipedia's complete roster of Roman emperors from Augustus in 27 BC to Constantine XI in 1453, organized by dynasty across Principate, Dominate, and Byzantine eras.

title: List of semiconductor fabrication plants
description: Wikipedia's running inventory of every chip fab, open and closed, with wafer size, process node, and monthly capacity. The reference when you want to know where TSMC, GlobalFoundries, or STMicro actually make things.

title: List of Stadiums by Capacity
description: Wikipedia's running tally of sports stadiums seating 40,000 or more, ranked by permanent capacity. Excludes race tracks, defunct venues, and temporary seating bumps.

title: List of Telephone Country Codes
description: Wikipedia's reference table of every ITU-assigned telephone country code, organized by world numbering zones 1–9. The map of who gets which +N prefix and why.

title: List of U.S. National Historic Landmarks by state
description: Wikipedia's state-by-state index into the 2,597 sites the National Park Service has designated as nationally significant. Entry point for digging into any particular state's NHLs.

title: List of World Rally Championship rallies
description: Wikipedia's running ledger of every rally that's counted toward the WRC since 1973, organized by location and by season. Tracks the rotation systems, the swaps, and the calendar's slow churn.

title: ListChallenges
description: Community site for taking and making list-based quizzes — how many of the IMDb Top 250 have you seen, etc. The check-the-box version of trivia.

title: Little Chips from Texas — Early History of the Microcontroller, Part 1
description: The Chip Letter on how Texas Instruments helped birth the microcontroller in the 1970s. Part one of a series on the chips hiding inside every washing machine and toy guitar.

title: LiveLingua Conjugation
description: LiveLingua's verb conjugation tool, covering Spanish, French, Italian, German, and Portuguese. Drills tenses across the major Romance languages plus German in one interface.

title: Lonely Planet
description: The travel publisher's storefront — guidebooks, Best in Travel lists, and destination inspiration sorted by continent, country, and city. The guidebook brand that defined backpacker shelves for decades.

title: Lose the Very
description: Tool that swaps 'very + [simple adjective]' for a sharper single word. Type 'very tired,' get 'exhausted.' Crowd-sourced thesaurus aimed at tightening prose.

title: Lotus 1-2-3 For Linux
description: Tavis Ormandy ports Lotus 1-2-3 natively to Linux thirty years late, recovering the lost LPL SDK from BBS warez tapes and hacking GNU objcopy along the way. One of the great reverse-engineering writeups.

title: macOSicons
description: Community archive of 30,000+ replacement icons for macOS apps, uploaded daily by users and downloadable as .icns or PNG. Built and run by Elías.

title: Magmidt
description: YouTube channel from Magmidt. URL-only classification — no page content available to identify the creator's focus.

title: Mahsa Amini protests
description: Wikipedia on the 2022–2023 uprising in Iran sparked by Mahsa Amini's death in morality police custody. The Woman, Life, Freedom movement — slogans, schoolgirl poisonings, executions, and the regime's communications blackouts.

title: Mali Empire
description: Wikipedia on the West African empire that ran from c. 1235 to 1610, founded by Sundiata Keita and made famously rich by Mansa Musa's pilgrimage. Covers the Manding state's government, gold-and-salt trade economy, and slow collapse.

title: Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
description: Wikipedia on the 1923–1946 League of Nations mandate that carved post-Ottoman Levant into Greater Lebanon, the Alawite State, Jabal Druze, and the rest. The administrative scaffolding behind modern Syria and Lebanon's borders.

title: Manjarno — case against Manjaro Linux
description: A running indictment of Manjaro Linux: expired SSL certs (five times and counting), held-back security patches, DDoSing the AUR. The counter-pitch to 'Arch with an installer.'

title: Map Games
description: Simon Vreman's collection of browser map games built to drill GeoGuessr-relevant trivia — chevron types, guardrails, bollards, dialing codes, province locations. Memorization aids disguised as quizzes.

title: Marathon des Sables
description: The 250km six-stage ultramarathon across the Moroccan Sahara, founded in 1986 by Patrick Bauer. Runners carry their own food for a week in the dunes.

title: Marita Camacho Quirós
description: Costa Rican supercentenarian who served as First Lady from 1962 to 1966 alongside president Francisco Orlich Bolmarcich. Died in 2025 at 114, the world's oldest former first lady.

title: Match Group sued over 'addictive' dating apps
description: NPR on the 2024 federal lawsuit accusing Tinder, Hinge, and the League of gamifying romance to hook paying subscribers. Six plaintiffs argue the apps are built to keep you swiping, not to get you off them.

title: Mate (drink)
description: Wikipedia on mate, the caffeine-rich yerba infusion shared from a gourd through a bombilla across Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil. Pre-Columbian Guaraní origins, first written up by Spanish colonizers in the 15th century.

title: Mauro Prosperi — lost in the Sahara
description: ABC News retells how Italian ultramarathoner Mauro Prosperi got blown 291km off course in the 1994 Marathon des Sables, surviving nine days in the Sahara on bat blood and his own urine.

title: MDE Community — Medellín expat & local meetup hub
description: Curated WhatsApp groups and events connecting expats, digital nomads, and locals in Medellín, with offshoots in Chiang Mai and Rio. 50+ communities sorted by sports, culture, wellness, and affinity.

title: Memenome — brainrot AI study tool
description: Upload a PDF and Memenome turns it into a brainrot-style explainer video hosted by characters like 3Blue1Bron. Gen Z study aid out of Irvine, leaning all the way into the bit.

title: Mercosur
description: Wikipedia on the South American customs union binding Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay — plus the saga of Venezuela's adhesion and suspension, and Bolivia's pending membership. Background for anyone tracking regional trade politics south of the equator.

title: Merdeka 118
description: The 678.9m megatall in Kuala Lumpur that took the Southeast Asia height crown from Saigon's Landmark 81 in 2021. Songket-pattern facade, PNB-funded, opened January 2024 after a decade of construction.

title: Metra
description: Wikipedia on Chicago's commuter rail system — 11 lines, 242 stations, ~38 million annual rides across the metro area. Operated by the RTA since 1984.

title: Metric Conversion Act of 1975
description: The U.S. law that declared metric the 'preferred' system for trade and commerce, then made conversion entirely voluntary. Reagan abolished the implementing board seven years later.

title: Mexia Supermarket — lost 1999 abandoned-store footage
description: Lost Media Wiki entry on partially lost VHS footage shot inside an abandoned supermarket in Mexia, Texas in 1999. Niche dead-mall archaeology for the lost-media crowd.

title: Microsoft Activation Scripts
description: The massgravel project — open-source scripts that activate Windows and Office via HWID, Ohook, TSforge, and Online KMS. 177k stars, the de facto piracy toolkit hiding in plain sight on GitHub.

title: Migingo Island
description: A 2,000 m² rock in Lake Victoria packed with 131 fishermen and contested between Kenya and Uganda. Population density rivals Manhattan; the draw is Nile perch.

title: Milei gifts Meloni a chainsaw doll of himself
description: Brazilian news report on Javier Milei handing Giorgia Meloni a doll of himself wielding his trademark chainsaw during her Buenos Aires visit, alongside his anti-woke speech.

title: mob-rule — Why do you think they call them counties?
description: Long-running community site for tracking every US and Canadian county you've set foot in. Cross the county line, count it; flying over doesn't qualify.

title: Modern Standard Arabic
description: Wikipedia on fusha, the formal pan-Arab register used in writing, broadcast media, and education across 24 countries. Background for the gap between the standard and the spoken dialects.

title: Mohegan Bluffs
description: 150-foot clay cliffs on the southern shore of Block Island, Rhode Island. Named for a mid-16th-century battle where the Niantic drove the Mohegans over the edge.

title: Money & Macro
description: YouTube channel from a Dutch macroeconomist breaking down central banks, currency crises, and global economic stories with charts and a calm, explainer cadence.

title: Monkey Thieves of Bali's Uluwatu Temple
description: WSJ feature on the macaques at Uluwatu Temple who snatch tourists' sunglasses and phones, then barter them back for fruit. A trained extortion racket with monkeys as the muscle.

title: Monroe Doctrine
description: Wikipedia on the 1823 U.S. foreign policy declaring the Western Hemisphere off-limits to European colonization. Traces the doctrine from Monroe through the Roosevelt Corollary, the Cold War, and a 21st-century 'Donroe' revival.

title: Montreal Is Actually Much Older Than Canada
description: Condé Nast Traveler riff on Montreal's 375th birthday in 2017 — French settlers in 1642, the Kanata etymology, Vieux-Montréal landmarks, and the city's first recorded tourist showing up in 1662.

title: Moorish Science Temple of America
description: Wikipedia on the Black American religious movement Noble Drew Ali founded in 1925, teaching that African Americans are Moorish by nationality and Muslim by faith. Precursor to the Nation of Islam and ancestor of today's Moorish sovereign citizen current.

title: Movements for U.S. Annexation of Canada
description: Wikipedia's running tally of every serious and unserious push to merge Canada into the United States, from the 1775 Invasion of Quebec through Trump's 51st-state rhetoric. Includes Albertan annexationism and the 1949 Newfoundland near-miss.

title: Multilingualism
description: Wikipedia's overview of using multiple languages — covers acquisition, cognitive effects, neuroscience, and how multilingual communities function around the world. The umbrella entry for everything bilingualism-adjacent.

title: Mundo Lingo
description: Free weekly language-exchange meetups that started in Buenos Aires in 2011 and spread to cities worldwide. Flag stickers on your shirt mark the languages you speak; strangers come talk to you.

title: Museu Paulista de Antiguidades Mecânicas
description: Wikipedia on Brazil's first antique car museum, founded by Roberto Lee in São Paulo in 1963 and now in Caçapava. Collection includes a 1948 Tucker Torpedo and the 1973 Ford Maverick from the first Raid da Integração Nacional.

title: Muslim conquest of the Maghreb
description: Wikipedia on the 647–709 AD Arab campaigns that pulled Byzantine North Africa under Umayyad rule. Covers the three invasions, the Berber revolts, and the long tail of Islamization across the region.

title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
description: Wikipedia on the Ottoman officer who won the Turkish War of Independence and founded the Republic of Turkey in 1923, then spent fifteen years dragging it toward secular modernity by decree.

title: Mutilated Currency — Federal Reserve / BEP
description: Federal Reserve explainer on what to do with badly damaged US currency. Points to the Bureau of Engraving and Printing's free redemption program, which pays out when more than 50% of a note is identifiable.

title: MyFitnessPal
description: Calorie and macro tracker with a 20-million-item food database, barcode scanning, and a freemium model gating intermittent fasting and custom macros behind Premium.

title: mystery-o-matic — daily murder mystery game
description: Free browser game serving a fresh procedurally-generated murder mystery every day. Cluedo meets Murdle, with each puzzle synthesized through random exploration rather than a fixed deduction path.

title: N. Korea cracks down on water park corruption — Daily NK
description: Daily NK report on Pyongyang prosecutors raiding the city's water parks over an organized ticket-scalping ring run with tacit approval from park officials squeezed for cash from above.

title: Naha Great Tug-of-War Festival
description: Annual Okinawan festival where East and West teams haul a 40-ton rope down Route 58 in Naha. Roots in 15th-century rain rituals; Guinness-certified as the world's largest tug-of-war since 1997.

title: Namhae German Village
description: A South Korean village built in 2001 to lure home Koreans who'd worked as nurses and miners in West Germany decades earlier. Now hosts an Oktoberfest that pulls in tens of thousands.

title: National Bank of Haiti
description: A French bank founded in Paris in 1881 by Crédit Industriel et Commercial to manage Haiti's currency and finish off the indemnity France extracted after the revolution. Shut down by President Antoine Simon in 1910.

title: National Diet
description: Japan's bicameral national legislature, founded in 1890 — the House of Representatives (lower) and House of Councillors (upper). Currently led by PM Sanae Takaichi of the LDP.

title: National Register of Historic Places listings
description: Wikipedia's index to NRHP listings across every U.S. state and territory, with current tallies as of August 2025. The jumping-off point for the 95,000+ buildings, sites, and districts on the federal register.

title: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia
description: Wikipedia on Operation Allied Force, NATO's 78-day 1999 air campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia during the Kosovo War. Ended with the Kumanovo Agreement, KFOR deployment, and Yugoslav withdrawal from Kosovo.

title: NAUPA — National Association of Unclaimed Property Administrators
description: The official network of US state treasurers running unclaimed property programs. Start here to find the legit state search portals before the scammy lookalikes.

title: Neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires
description: Wikipedia's index of the 48 official barrios that make up the autonomous city, with population, area, and commune for each. Includes the informal neighbourhoods locals use but the city doesn't.

title: Neutral Colors in Design
description: Design Bootcamp piece on Medium about working with neutral color palettes — the grays, off-whites, and beiges that hold UI together. Post is gone (410), so going off the slug.

title: New 7 Wonders of the World
description: Wikipedia on the 2007 online popularity poll that crowned Chichén Itzá, Christ the Redeemer, the Great Wall, Machu Picchu, Petra, the Taj Mahal, and the Colosseum. Run by a Swiss foundation, dismissed as unscientific, embraced by tourism boards anyway.

title: Niagara Falls peace conference
description: The 1914 ABC Powers mediation — Argentina, Brazil, and Chile brokering between the US and Huerta's Mexico after the Veracruz occupation. A rare moment of South American great-power diplomacy.

title: Nicco Loves Linux
description: YouTube channel covering Linux, open source, and KDE development, with a side of politics and activism. Desktop Linux enthusiast content from a contributor's-eye view.

title: Nintendo PlayStation — unreleased SNES-CD prototype
description: PlayStation Fandom wiki entry on the Nintendo PlayStation, the aborted SNES-CD console Sony and Nintendo co-developed before the deal collapsed and Sony went solo with the PS1.

title: No Upside for Supreme Court in Deciding Elections
description: Jess Bravin in the WSJ on why the Court has nothing to gain from refereeing presidential elections, drawing the line from Bush v. Gore in 2000 to the 2024 Trump ballot cases.

title: Nomad Groups — digital nomad community directory
description: Searchable database of WhatsApp and Telegram groups for digital nomads, sorted by city and continent. Built by Diogo Matos and Martin Macek as a side project.

title: Nomads.com — digital nomad city rankings
description: Pieter Levels' ranking of cities for remote workers, scored on cost, internet, weather, and safety. Formerly Nomad List; the original aggregator of the genre since 2014.

title: nomadtable — meet fellow travelers app
description: iOS/Android app for solo travelers to browse nearby activities — coffees, parties, rooftop drinks — and join one to meet other people in the same city. Built by a solo traveler.

title: North American Numbering Plan
description: Wikipedia on the NANP — the unified country-code-1 telephone system covering the US, Canada, and most of the Caribbean. Origins in AT&T's 1940s Operator Toll Dialing scheme.

title: Nova classification
description: Brazilian framework that sorts food into four groups by degree of processing, from whole ingredients to ultra-processed products. Carlos Monteiro's 2009 paper out of the University of São Paulo, now standard in nutrition policy worldwide.

title: Nova Petrópolis
description: Small municipality in Rio Grande do Sul's Serra Gaúcha, settled by German-Brazilian immigrants who still speak Riograndenser Hunsrückisch. Markets itself as the Garden of Serra Gaúcha; tourism, wool, and dairy keep it running.

title: Novgorod Republic
description: Wikipedia on the medieval Russian city-state (1136–1478) governed by veche assembly and elected posadnik until Ivan III absorbed it into Moscow. A rare republican experiment in Rus' history.

title: ntfy.sh — HTTP push notification service
description: Pub-sub notification service you hit with a curl PUT to ntfy.sh/yourtopic and get a push on your phone. Open source, self-hostable, no account required for basic use.

title: Nürburgring
description: The German race track in the Eifel mountains, nicknamed "The Green Hell" by Jackie Stewart. Home of the 20.8-km Nordschleife — the benchmark every production car gets timed against.

title: Obesity in Mexico
description: Wikipedia on how Mexico went from malnutrition to seven-in-ten overweight in a generation, driven by transnational food companies displacing the traditional diet since the 1980s.

title: Observatory of Economic Complexity
description: OEC visualizes international trade flows across 190+ countries, 8,200+ products, and thousands of firms — tree maps, networks, and rankings built on UN Comtrade data. The reference dashboard for who exports what to whom.

title: Occitan language
description: Wikipedia on the Romance language of southern France, Monaco, and parts of Italy and Spain — the tongue of the troubadours, now down to a few hundred thousand active speakers.

title: Old Online Chevy Manuals
description: Keith Hardy's archive of 370+ pre-1980 Chevrolet and GMC manuals, bulletins, and booklets — 26,400+ pages, free, hosted under the Old Car Manual Project. Active again after a decade quiet, now extending coverage through the 1970s.

title: Open Food Facts
description: Collaborative open database of 914,000+ food products — ingredients, nutrition facts, Nutri-Score, NOVA group, Green-Score. Wikipedia-model for the supermarket aisle, built by volunteers and free to reuse.

title: OpenWrt's Future-Proof Reference Hardware
description: Ars Technica on OpenWrt turning 20 and proposing the OpenWrt One — a sub-$100 reference router with battery-backed RTC, USB-PD, and no binary blobs. Banana Pi builds it; donations go to SFC.

title: Operation Condor
description: The US-backed campaign of political repression and state terror waged by South America's Southern Cone dictatorships in the 1970s and 80s. Wikipedia's deep-dive into the cross-border kidnappings, disassinations, and the long tail of prosecutions.

title: Operation Monopoly
description: The FBI's 1977 plan to tunnel under the new Soviet Embassy in DC for signals intelligence. Leaks, bad blueprints, and zero usable intel — exposed in 2001 by Robert Hanssen.

title: Operation Yellow Ribbon
description: Canada's emergency response to 9/11, diverting 200+ grounded US-bound flights to Canadian airports. Gander, Newfoundland alone took 38 airliners and 6,595 stranded passengers.

title: Optical phenomenon
description: Wikipedia's taxonomy of observable light-matter interactions, from rainbows and 22° halos to entoptic floaters and unexplained sightings. Sorts the atmospheric from the perceptual from the genuinely weird.

title: Pacific Crest Trail
description: The 2,653-mile National Scenic Trail running from the Mexican border at Campo, California to Manning Park, British Columbia. Climbs to 13,153 feet at Forester Pass in the Sierra.

title: Pamir Mountains
description: Wikipedia on the high mountain range where the Tian Shan, Karakoram, Kunlun, Hindu Kush, and Himalayas meet — the 'Roof of the World' straddling Tajikistan, Afghanistan, China, and Kyrgyzstan.

title: Pavel Durov
description: Wikipedia on the Russian-born founder of VK and Telegram. Holds four citizenships, claims 100+ biological children, got indicted in France in 2024 over Telegram moderation.

title: Peanut Hole — international waters in the Sea of Okhotsk
description: The peanut-shaped pocket of international waters at the center of the Sea of Okhotsk, surrounded by Russia's EEZ. A textbook straddling-stock and tragedy-of-the-commons case until Russia claimed the seabed in 2014.

title: Pekingology
description: CSIS podcast unpacking Chinese politics and the inner workings of the Communist Party. Hosted by Henrietta Levin of the Freeman Chair in China Studies.

title: Perestroika
description: Gorbachev's late-1980s restructuring of the Soviet economy and political system. The reforms meant to save the USSR that ended up dismantling it — paired with glasnost, contrasted with China's Deng-era path.

title: Persepolis
description: Wikipedia on the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire, founded by Darius I around 518 BC and burned by Alexander in 330 BC. The ruins sit near Shiraz in modern Fars province.

title: Peter Santenello
description: YouTube channel where Santenello drops into communities most travel vloggers skip — Appalachia, Native reservations, Chicano LA, the Amish — with a GoPro and no editorial angle. Long-form portraits, locals doing the talking.

title: Photography Basics
description: Photography Life's beginner course covering exposure, composition, and camera fundamentals. Long-running tutorial hub run by Nasim Mansurov, aimed at people picking up a camera for the first time.

title: Plan 9 from Bell Labs
description: Bell Labs' research OS designed as the successor to Unix, built around the 9P protocol and the everything-is-a-file-server idea taken to its logical conclusion. Now MIT-licensed, still kicking via the Plan 9 Foundation.

title: PlatesMania — world license plate database
description: User-contributed photo database of license plates from around the world. Browse by country, search by plate number, or post your own sightings.

title: Plaza Accord
description: The 1985 agreement where France, West Germany, Japan, the UK, and the US met at New York's Plaza Hotel to deliberately depreciate the dollar. The pivot point for understanding 80s currency politics and Japan's lost decade.

title: Plonkit — GeoGuessr meta guide
description: The community-built guide to GeoGuessr clues — bollards, road lines, utility poles, license plates, country by country. The reference serious players actually use.

title: PMC article — PMC10032309
description: A biomedical research article archived in PubMed Central, NIH's open-access repository for life-sciences literature. Specific subject unknown — the page served a browser-verification wall instead of content.

title: Pod.link — podcast share-link redirector
description: Pod.link resolves a podcast to every major app — Apple, Spotify, Overcast, Pocket Casts — from one URL. ID 1587816694 points to a specific show, but the page didn't load.

title: pod.link — universal podcast link
description: Pod.link resolves a podcast to whichever app the visitor uses — Apple, Spotify, Overcast, Pocket Casts. This specific link (ID 1150510297) points to a show but the page bot-walled, so the show itself is unidentified.

title: Pod.link podcast share page
description: Pod.link landing page for a podcast (Apple Podcasts ID 1460154838), routing listeners to their app of choice. Which show specifically is unclear without the page content.

title: Poland has changed beyond recognition
description: Anna Gromada traces Poland's leap from 13:1 GDP gap with Germany in 1989 to European high-achiever, told through her own family's arc from shadow-economy farm labour to professional class.

title: Poland unveils 'Tusk Line' defences to protect Europe
description: Telegraph dispatch on Poland fortifying its eastern border with Belarus and Kaliningrad — bunkers, anti-tank barriers, surveillance — pitched as Europe's forward shield against Russia.

title: Poland: Paths of Glory or Roads to Perdition?
description: 2013 CNBC piece on Poland's EU-funded road-building boom — motorways doubled in five years, yet drivers still die at nearly twice the EU rate. The modernization-vs-safety tension.

title: Polski Fiat
description: Polish car brand that built Fiats under license from 1932 — first at the state-owned PZInż works in Warsaw, later at FSO with the 125p and the tiny 126p that motorized communist Poland.

title: Pomerode
description: Brazilian municipality in Santa Catarina founded by Pomeranian settlers in 1861, billed as the most German town in Brazil. Locals still speak East Pomeranian Low German alongside Portuguese.

title: Portuguese Dialects
description: Wikipedia's overview of the regional variations of Portuguese across Europe, South America, Africa, and Asia. Covers conservative vs. innovative features, dialect-specific homophones, and mutual intelligibility with Galician.

title: Portuguese Empire
description: Wikipedia's sweep of the first global colonial empire, from Ceuta in 1415 to Macau's handover in 1999. Six centuries spanning Brazil, Goa, Malacca, Angola, and the spice routes that rewired world trade.

title: Portuguese Riviera
description: The affluent coastal stretch west of Lisbon — Cascais, Estoril, Oeiras, Sintra. Became a refuge for exiled European royalty during and after WWII, and never really shook the reputation.

title: Potential enlargement of the European Union
description: Wikipedia's running tracker of EU accession candidates — Western Balkans, the Association Trio, Turkey — plus internal secession scenarios like Catalonia and the fate of Greenland.

title: PPPeter
description: YouTube channel from PPPeter, a Chinese-Canadian pianist and content creator known for piano covers, viral keyboard challenges, and music memes. Built a following on visually flashy MIDI-style performances.

title: Prague's narrowest street — Metro travel piece
description: Metro reporter visits Vinárna Čertovka, the 50cm-wide alley in Malá Strana that TikTok turned into a queue. Verdict: tourist trap, traffic lights and all.

title: Probably Robbed in Brazil
description: Travel blog post from Two Cats Backpack about close calls and near-misses across Rio, São Paulo, and Salvador. Half cautionary tale, half love letter to Brazil's chaos.

title: Prohibition in Canada
description: The Canadian Encyclopedia's entry on Canada's temperance-driven booze ban, from 19th-century church-basement organizing through the patchwork provincial repeal that left Prince Edward Island dry until 1948.

title: Project Based Learning
description: GitHub's index of project-based programming tutorials, sorted by language. The place to go when you've done the intro course and need something to actually build.

title: Pseudo-anglicism
description: Wikipedia on words that look English but aren't — baby-foot, shake-hand, rallye-paper. The lexical borrowing pattern where a language reworks English parts into something English speakers wouldn't recognize.

title: Psychedelics and the Default Mode Network
description: Jasmine Virdi explains how LSD, psilocybin, and ayahuasca quiet the brain's default mode network — the introspective circuit that constitutes the ego — and why that 'reboot' drives their therapeutic effects.

title: Psychology with Dr. Ana
description: YouTube channel from a clinical psychology doctorate holder and fiction author, breaking down relationships, personality, and evidence-based psych for a general audience.

title: Public Housing in Singapore
description: Wikipedia on the HDB system that houses ~80% of Singaporeans. Traces the arc from 1930s SIT tenements through Lee-era resettlement blocks to today's asset-enhancement regime.

title: Pyongyang Marathon
description: Wikipedia on North Korea's annual April marathon, running from Kim Il Sung Stadium along the Taedong River since 1981. Opened to foreign amateurs in 2000 — one of the only ways tourists legally enter the DPRK.

title: Pyramiden
description: Abandoned Soviet coal-mining town on Svalbard, founded by Sweden in 1910, sold to the USSR in 1927, shuttered in 1998. The Arctic cold preserved the Lenin bust, the gym, and the propaganda intact.

title: Qingdao
description: Wikipedia on the Shandong port city the Germans built into a treaty colony — hence the brewery, the red-roofed downtown, and Tsingtao beer. Later Japanese-occupied, now a 10-million metro and 2008 Olympic sailing venue.

title: Queenstown's road cone problem
description: WSJ on how New Zealand's tourist boomtown ended up drowning in orange traffic cones. A workplace-culture story about overzealous safety contracting dressed as a quirky travel dispatch.

title: Quick guide to Beirut's best neighbourhoods
description: Lonely Planet's neighborhood-by-neighborhood rundown of Beirut — Gemmayzeh, Mar Mikhael, Hamra, and the rest. Standard travel-mag framing, useful for first-time orientation.

title: Quiraing
description: A landslip-formed landform on the Trotternish escarpment of Skye, with named features like the Needle, the Table, and the Prison. Alexander Smith called it "a nightmare of nature."

title: Quote of the Day — Guido Fawkes
description: Westminster gossip blog Guido Fawkes runs a 2011 Berlusconi soundbite: the Italian PM admits a 25% homosexual quotient after 'profound examination.' Pure Silvio.

title: Race and ethnicity in Brazil
description: Wikipedia's overview of how Brazil's Indigenous, Portuguese, African, Italian, Spanish, German, Lebanese, and Japanese strands fused — and how the state and ideologues from Oliveira Vianna to Gilberto Freyre tried to make sense of the mix.

title: Railway Oriented Programming
description: Scott Wlaschin's talk and slides framing functional error handling as a two-track railway, with F# and C# code on GitHub. The canonical pitch for ROP, plus his own later caveat against taking it too far.

title: Rain In The UAE — Cloud Seeding Explained
description: Grazia Middle East explainer on how the UAE manufactures rain by firing salt flares into clouds. Covers the NCM's program, NASA collaborations, and why the Gulf's clouds are unusually hard to seed.

title: Raising of Chicago
description: How 1850s Chicago jacked its entire downtown several feet into the air to install a sewer system. Buildings stayed open for business while crews cranked them up on screwjacks.

title: ranlab
description: Pulls a random project from Awesome-Selfhosted so you have something new to deploy in your homelab. Built because the author was bored and had nothing left to self-host.

title: RAS syndrome
description: Wikipedia on the redundant use of an acronym alongside one of its own words — "PIN number," "ATM machine," "HIV virus." The term itself is autological: redundant acronym syndrome syndrome.

title: Recreational Drug Tourism
description: Wikipedia survey of travel undertaken to obtain or use drugs unavailable, illegal, or pricier back home. Region-by-region tour from Malana charas to Amsterdam coffee shops to Bolivian cocaine bars.

title: Rednaxela Terrace
description: Tiny pedestrian street in Hong Kong's Mid-Levels whose name is just "Alexander" spelled backwards — a relic of right-to-left Chinese transliteration. José Rizal lived at No. 2 in 1891.

title: Rent a Trabi Budapest
description: Budapest sightseeing tours in two-stroke Trabants, the cardboard wonder of East German motoring. Communist-era kitsch on wheels — pick from the Communist Tour, Retro Tour, or one fueled by Unicum.

title: Republic of Ragusa
description: Wikipedia on the maritime republic centered on Dubrovnik, 1358–1808. Outlasted Venetian and Ottoman suzerainty by playing tribute states off each other, motto: liberty isn't for sale at any price.

title: Republic of Vevčani
description: A North Macedonian village declared itself a micronation in 1991 after the Yugoslav government tried to redirect its spring water. Red passports, harlequin-and-cauldron flag, souvenir currency.

title: Risk
description: The 1957 Albert Lamorisse war game where you push armies across 42 territories and try to take the world. Dice, alliances, and the long afternoons that follow.

title: Roam like at home — EU mobile roaming policy
description: European Parliament explainer on the EU rule that killed mobile roaming charges across the 27 member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. Extended in 2022 for another decade.

title: Roaring Twenties
description: Wikipedia's overview of the 1920s decade of economic boom, jazz, flappers, Prohibition, and Harlem Renaissance across the US and Europe — ending at Black Tuesday.

title: Robert Moses
description: Wikipedia biography of the unelected master builder who shaped 20th-century New York through parkways, bridges, parks, and slum clearance. The villain of Caro's Power Broker.

title: Robert Pope (runner)
description: British vet who spent 422 days running 15,700 miles across the US — four crossings — to retrace Forrest Gump's fictional route. Also holds the Guinness record for fastest marathon dressed as a film character.

title: RobWords
description: YouTube channel from Rob Watts on the quirks of English — etymology, lost letters, pronunciation drift, and why spelling is a mess. Former BBC journalist doing pop linguistics with a presenter's polish.

title: Roland TR-808
description: Wikipedia on Roland's 1980 drum machine — a commercial flop that became the backbone of hip-hop, electro, and house once its booming analog kick hit the used market.

title: Roman citizenship
description: Wikipedia on civitas — the legal status that structured rights, property, and political life in ancient Rome. Walks through the tiered system (Cives Romani, Latini, Socii, Peregrini) up to Caracalla's 212 AD edict extending citizenship empire-wide.

title: Roman Empire
description: Wikipedia's main article on the Roman Empire, from Augustus through the fall of the West and the Eastern survival as Byzantium. Covers government, military, economy, daily life, and the long afterlife.

title: Roman province
description: Wikipedia on the administrative units Rome carved its empire into, from Republican-era provincia to the late imperial dioceses. Includes the full chronological roster province by province.

title: Romani language
description: Wikipedia on the Indo-Aryan macrolanguage of the Romani people, with roughly 4.6 million speakers across a sprawl of dialects from the Balkans to the British Isles. Heavy on phonology, morphology, and the contact-language mess that comes with a thousand-year diaspora.

title: Romania: Potential Unlocked
description: Global Finance Magazine country report on Romania — economic outlook, investment climate, and the structural reforms unlocking its growth potential.

title: Rook to XSS
description: Skii chains a chess-themed bug into cross-site scripting. Personal security blog writeup, the kind of thing that lands on r/netsec for an afternoon.

title: Round Barns in Illinois
description: Wikipedia on the multiple-property NRHP submission covering 18 round barns across Illinois. Stephenson County holds the densest cluster, and the University of Illinois experiment station drove the design's Midwest spread.

title: Royal Mail minded to accept £3.5bn takeover offer
description: Telegraph report on Royal Mail's board signaling acceptance of Daniel Křetínský's £3.5bn bid. The 508-year-old British postal institution headed for Czech ownership.

title: Russian court fines Google $2 decillion
description: A Russian court ordered Google to pay roughly $20 decillion for YouTube banning ultra-nationalist channels like Tsargrad and Zvezda. The fine doubles weekly — more money than exists on Earth.

title: Russian Grammar — alphaDictionary
description: Robert Beard's reference grammar of Russian, covering declensions, conjugations, and pronunciation. Old-school academic linguistics site from the Bucknell professor behind alphaDictionary.

title: Russian intervention in the Syrian civil war
description: Wikipedia on Moscow's nine-year air campaign propping up Assad, from the September 2015 deployment to the regime's collapse in December 2024. Ends with the opposition victory Russia spent a decade trying to prevent.

title: Russian Terms Derived from French — Wiktionary category
description: Wiktionary's index of 1,738 Russian words traced back to French — абажур, абонемент, авеню, амплуа and the rest of the Gallicisms that flooded in during the 18th–19th centuries.

title: Sam Houston
description: Wikipedia biography of the 19th-century general and statesman who led the Texas Revolution, served as president of the Republic of Texas, then governor of both Tennessee and Texas — the only person to govern two U.S. states.

title: Sam's Club
description: Walmart-owned membership warehouse club. Bulk groceries, electronics, and tires behind a paywall — the Costco competitor with thinner crowds and a worse hot dog.

title: Samarkand
description: Wikipedia on the ancient Silk Road city in Uzbekistan — Timur's capital, home to the Registan and Ulugh Beg's observatory. One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia.

title: Sanskrit
description: Wikipedia's deep dive on the classical Indo-Aryan language of the Vedas, Pāṇini's grammar, and most Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain liturgy. Covers Vedic through Classical, the Prakrit split, and Sanskrit's reach across South and Southeast Asia.

title: São Miguel das Missões
description: Wikipedia entry on the Rio Grande do Sul municipality built around 17th-century Spanish Jesuit mission ruins. UNESCO-listed since 1983 as part of the Jesuit Missions of the Guaranis.

title: Seattle Underground
description: Network of buried passageways and basements under Pioneer Square, left behind when Seattle regraded its streets one to two stories up after the 1889 Great Fire. Now a guided tourist crawl beneath the sidewalks.

title: Seattle's Bike Network Can't Handle Its Own Popularity
description: The Urbanist on how SDOT's flagship protected bike lanes are designed for yesterday's ridership — two-bike waiting boxes, undersized lanes — even as the city's climate plan targets 7% bike mode share by 2030.

title: Sebastião Salgado
description: Brazilian social documentary photographer (1944–2025) who shot in 120+ countries, from Serra Pelada gold miners to the Genesis project. UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, Académie des Beaux-Arts member.

title: Second Congo War
description: Wikipedia on the 1998–2003 war that pulled nine African nations into the DRC and killed millions. Called Africa's World War for a reason — the deadliest conflict since WWII.

title: Securing the Baltic Power Grid
description: IEEE Spectrum on the Baltic states' 2025 disconnect from the Russian grid and synchronization with continental Europe. The engineering and geopolitics of cutting a Soviet-era electrical umbilical.

title: Security incidents involving Barack Obama
description: Wikipedia's running catalog of threats, plots, and breaches targeting Obama from 2007 onward — Waffle House plots, White House fence-jumpers, the 2018 mail bombs, Taranto's 2023 arrest.

title: Seine-Port's smartphone ban
description: Guardian dispatch from Seine-Port, a French village of under 2,000 that voted by referendum to ban scrolling in streets, shops, parks, and cafes. Teens admit there's not much else to do.

title: Senegalese tea culture
description: Wikipedia on attaya, the three-glass Senegalese tea ritual where Chinese green tea, mint, and sugar get poured back and forth from a height until the foam thickens. Slow on purpose — that's the social point.

title: Serapis flag
description: The unconventional 1779 U.S. ensign John Paul Jones flew on his captured British frigate after the Bonhomme Richard sank with its colors. Red, white, and blue stripes — the Dutch sketched it to dodge calling him a pirate.

title: Sestertius
description: Wikipedia on the ancient Roman coin worth two and a half asses — small silver in the Republic, large brass under the Empire. Where the HS shorthand and the IIS symbol come from.

title: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
description: The seven monumental structures of classical antiquity — Great Pyramid, Hanging Gardens, Colossus of Rhodes, and the rest. The canonical list comes from a 1572 book, not antiquity itself.

title: Sewers of Toronto — Atlas Obscura
description: Atlas Obscura entry on Toronto's underground sewer system, the kind of buried infrastructure urban explorers chase. Part of the site's catalog of overlooked subterranean spaces.

title: Sharks off Rio de Janeiro test positive for cocaine
description: Reuters on a Fiocruz study finding cocaine in 13 Brazilian sharpnose sharks off Rio, traced to sewage runoff, clandestine refining, and traffickers' jettisoned bricks.

title: Sheriff — Transnistria's monopoly conglomerate
description: Wikipedia on Sheriff, the company that owns nearly everything profitable in breakaway Transnistria. Founded in 1993 by two ex-KGB officers; runs the supermarkets, the petrol stations, the TV channel, and FC Sheriff Tiraspol.

title: Shibam
description: The walled mud-brick city in Yemen's Wadi Hadhramaut, nicknamed Manhattan of the Desert for its 16th-century tower houses. UNESCO World Heritage site, on the endangered list since 2015.

title: Shibam — Manhattan of the Desert
description: National Geographic profile of Shibam, the 16th-century Yemeni walled city of mud-brick high-rises rising seven stories above Wadi Hadramaut. Freya Stark coined the nickname in the 1930s.

title: shiey
description: YouTube channel of shiey, a Slovak filmmaker who freight-hops trains across Europe and Asia and films the journeys. Slow, atmospheric travel docs from places most travel vloggers skip.

title: SHIFTphone 8
description: Modular Android phone from German maker SHIFT — IP66-rated, repairable with a screwdriver, dual 50MP cameras, and a swappable universal battery shared across SHIFT devices.

title: Should I Open Source my Company?
description: Supabase CTO Ant Wilson on why open-sourcing the company turned out to be one of their best decisions. Walks through the usual founder fears — bad code, security holes, IP theft — and the unexpected upsides.

title: Siam Di Tella
description: Argentine metalworking giant founded by Torcuato di Tella in 1911, from bread machines to Siambretta scooters to licensed Morris-based cars. Bankrupt by 1981; the SIAM brand was relaunched in 2014.

title: Signalling System No. 7
description: Wikipedia on SS7, the 1970s ITU-T telephony signaling stack that still routes calls, SMS, and number portability across the global PSTN — and leaks location and 2FA codes to anyone with carrier access.

title: Silvio Berlusconi
description: Wikipedia on the Italian media tycoon who built Fininvest, founded Forza Italia, and served four terms as prime minister between scandals, trials, and Bunga Bunga. Died 2023.

title: Sinitic languages
description: Wikipedia on the Sinitic branch of Sino-Tibetan — Mandarin, Yue, Hakka, Min, Wu, Hui, Gan, Xiang, plus the contested Macro-Bai. Covers classification fights and the writing-system, phonology, and grammar splits across the group.

title: Sivalik Hills
description: Wikipedia on the outer Himalayan foothills running 2,400 km from the Indus to the Brahmaputra. Tertiary sandstone packed with Neogene-Pleistocene vertebrate fossils and the Soanian Paleolithic culture.

title: Slate's electric truck — price, paint, radio details
description: The Verge breaks down Slate Auto's bare-bones electric pickup: Bezos-backed, sub-$30K, no paint options, no touchscreen radio. The anti-Cybertruck pitch.

title: Sleep Deprivation Amps Up the Brain
description: Scientific American on Marcello Massimini's TMS study showing the brain grows more electrically jumpy the longer you stay awake. Explains why all-nighters help depressives and trigger seizures in epileptics.

title: Smuggler Caught With 420 M.2 SSDs Strapped to His Stomach
description: Tom's Hardware on a Hong Kong customs bust: a man crossing into mainland China with 420 M.2 SSDs taped to his torso, roughly $32,000 in storage. Peak gray-market silicon smuggling.

title: Songkran
description: Thailand's traditional New Year, observed April 13–16 with water-pouring rituals, sand stupas, and the famous nationwide water fights. UNESCO inscribed it as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2023.

title: South America's Electric Car Surge — From Lagging To Accelerating
description: Michael Barnard's CleanTechnica analysis of South America's EV inflection: Brazil, Uruguay, and Colombia crossed the 5% sales threshold in 2024. Part of his global tipping-points series.

title: Sovereign Military Order of Malta
description: Wikipedia on the Catholic lay religious order descended from the medieval Knights Hospitaller. A sovereign entity with no territory, observer status at the UN, and its own passports and stamps.

title: Sovereign State of the Bektashi Order
description: Wikipedia on the proposed Bektashi microstate inside Tirana — an 11-hectare enclave that would undercut the Vatican as the world's smallest sovereign state. Edi Rama's pitch, Baba Mondi's order.

title: Soviet Embassy's Identity Crisis
description: Washington Post dispatch from December 1991 on the Soviet Embassy in DC unraveling alongside the USSR itself — ethnic splits, money woes, and Yeltsin's man quietly seizing staff from the ambassador.

title: Soviet invasion of Manchuria
description: Wikipedia on the August 1945 Soviet campaign that shattered the Kwantung Army in three weeks and set up the partition of Korea at the 38th parallel.

title: Soviet War Films — Wikipedia category
description: Wikipedia's index of Soviet war cinema, sorted into subcategories (WWI, WWII, propaganda, drama, comedy) plus 34 standalone titles from Fall of Berlin to Stalingrad (1943).

title: Spanish With Nate
description: YouTube channel from Nate, a high-school-Spanish-kid-turned-evangelist, teaching the language to English speakers. Pitch leans hard on the social-life upside of getting conversational.

title: Spartan Race
description: Wikipedia on the obstacle-race franchise Joe De Sena spun off from his 48-hour Death Race in 2010. Sprint to 50k ultra, now in 30 countries.

title: Special Economic Zones of China
description: Wikipedia on the SEZs Deng Xiaoping carved out starting in 1980 — Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou, Xiamen, later Hainan, Pudong, Binhai. The laboratory where China ran its market-reform experiments.

title: Spinnaker Tower
description: 170-metre observation tower at Portsmouth Harbour, opened 2005 and shaped like a billowing sail. Portsmouth residents picked the design from three options in a 1998 public poll.

title: SQL Murder Mystery
description: Northwestern Knight Lab's SQLite whodunnit — you query a fake police database to solve a murder in SQL City. Equal parts SQL practice and detective game, with a walkthrough for beginners.

title: State of Scott
description: Scott County, Tennessee responded to Tennessee's 1861 secession by declaring itself a 'Free and Independent State' loyal to the Union. It didn't get around to formally rescinding the act until 1986.

title: State of Syria
description: The French Mandate state stitched together from Aleppo and Damascus in 1925, lasting just five years before the Great Syrian Revolt forced its conversion into the First Syrian Republic. Interwar cartography at its messiest.

title: Steve Kaufmann — lingosteve
description: YouTube channel of Steve Kaufmann, polyglot co-founder of LingQ, on how to learn languages. Twenty languages deep, evangelizing input-based acquisition over classroom drills.

title: StoryLearning
description: Olly Richards's YouTube channel on learning languages through stories rather than grammar drills. Companion to his StoryLearning method and the I Will Teach You A Language brand.

title: Stossel TV
description: John Stossel's YouTube channel — the former ABC and Fox Business correspondent posts short libertarian explainers on regulation, economics, and government overreach.

title: Strava Bans User for Running in North Korea
description: DC Rainmaker unpacks Strava's account-termination policy after a PhD researcher's Pyongyang Marathon run synced from Garmin Connect got their account nuked. Even treadmill runs spoofed to North Korea trigger it.

title: Sun dog
description: Wikipedia on the atmospheric optical phenomenon — bright spots flanking the sun at 22°, formed by sunlight refracting through ice crystals. Also called parhelia, with a history stretching back to antiquity and the Wars of the Roses.

title: Sun of May
description: Wikipedia on the radiant sun emblem on Argentina and Uruguay's flags, named for the May Revolution of 1810. The Inca-sun-god origin story is popular but unsupported by contemporary sources — the design traces to European heraldry's sun in splendour.

title: Surzhyk
description: Wikipedia on the Ukrainian–Russian mixed vernacular spoken across Ukraine and borderlands. Covers the Soviet-era stigma, regional variation, and the ethnopolitical baggage the label still carries.

title: Syria
description: Wikipedia's country article on Syria, spanning antiquity through the Ba'athist era to the post-2024 transitional period after the regime's fall. The reference baseline before reading anything else.

title: Syrian Kurdistan
description: Wikipedia on the Kurdish-inhabited region of northern Syria, also called Western Kurdistan or Rojava. Covers the Ottoman roots, French mandate years, Ba'athist suppression, and the autonomous administration that emerged from the civil war.

title: Tadeusz Kościuszko
description: Wikipedia on the Polish-Lithuanian military engineer who fortified West Point for the Continental Army, then went home and led the 1794 uprising against partition. Died in Swiss exile, 1817.

title: Taiga
description: Wikipedia on the boreal forest biome — the world's largest land biome, ringing the subarctic from 50°N to 70°N across Canada, Russia, and Scandinavia. Pines, spruces, larches, and not much else.

title: Taiping Island
description: Wikipedia on the largest natural Spratly island, administered by Taiwan from 1,400 km away and claimed by China, Vietnam, and the Philippines. A 46-hectare flashpoint in the South China Sea.

title: Tall poppy syndrome
description: Wikipedia on the Australian and New Zealand habit of cutting down peers who get too successful. Traces the phrase back to Livy's story of Tarquinius Superbus sweeping the heads off his garden poppies.

title: Tally marks
description: Wikipedia on the unary counting notation — the five-barred gate and its global variants. Traces the practice back 30,000 years to notched Aurignacian bones like the Wolf bone and Ishango bone.

title: Talon Fitness
description: YouTube channel from Talon, a strength and conditioning coach posting training breakdowns and fitness programming content.

title: Tangier International Zone
description: Wikipedia on the 1925–1956 international condominium that governed Tangier under a committee of European powers. A weird interwar experiment in shared sovereignty, swallowed back into Morocco at independence.

title: Technology Connections
description: Alec Watson's YouTube channel on the engineering history of everyday appliances — toasters, traffic lights, dishwashers, dehumidifiers. Long, patient explainers that make mundane hardware fascinating.

title: Ted Kaczynski
description: Wikipedia on the Unabomber — Harvard math prodigy turned Montana hermit who mailed bombs for seventeen years to protest industrial society. Author of the 35,000-word manifesto that got him caught when his brother recognized the prose.

title: Tempora — GCHQ internet surveillance system
description: GCHQ's fibre-optic tap that buffers most internet traffic for later searching. Operational since late 2011, exposed by Snowden in 2013 as the UK counterpart to NSA's bulk collection.

title: Terence McKenna
description: Wikipedia on the American ethnobotanist and psychedelic evangelist (1946–2000). Covers the stoned ape theory, Timewave Zero, machine elves, and the DMT-fueled lecture circuit that made him a countercultural fixture.

title: Texas Declaration of Causes of Secession
description: The 1861 document Texas issued explaining why it was leaving the Union, hosted by the Texas State Library. It is unambiguous about slavery being the reason — primary-source reading for anyone told otherwise.

title: Texas Declaration of Independence
description: Wikipedia on the 1836 proclamation that severed Texas from Mexico, drafted by George Childress at Washington-on-the-Brazos and signed by 60 delegates the day after.

title: Texas Revolution
description: Wikipedia on the 1835–1836 rebellion that broke Texas away from Santa Anna's Centralist Mexico. Six months from the first shot at Gonzales to Santa Anna's capture at San Jacinto.

title: The 50th Law
description: 2009 collaboration between Robert Greene and 50 Cent — a semi-autobiographical strategy book on fearlessness, threading 50's Southside Queens hustle through lessons from Sun Tzu, Lincoln, Socrates, and Malcolm X.

title: The B1M
description: YouTube channel covering large-scale construction and civil engineering — supertall towers, megaprojects, infrastructure disasters. Fred Mills hosts, with the polish of a documentary studio rather than a hobbyist channel.

title: The BeOS Bible
description: Scot Hacker's 1999 doorstop on BeOS, the multimedia-focused OS that briefly threatened to become the Mac alternative before Apple bought NeXT instead. Scanned and searchable at the Internet Archive.

title: The Big Red Word vs. the Little Green Man
description: Julia Turner in Slate on the 25-year standoff between America's red EXIT sign and Yukio Ota's green running-man pictogram. A small design fight that maps neatly onto bigger ones — metric, road signs, pictograms vs. words.

title: The Design Flaw That Almost Wiped Out an NYC Skyscraper
description: Slate cross-post of a 99% Invisible episode on Citicorp Center's hidden structural flaw — chevron bracing that couldn't handle quartering winds, fixed in secret welding sessions after hours.

title: The Friendliest City in Brazil — Belo Horizonte
description: Jason Daniel Shaw's travelogue from Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais — Brazil's first planned modern city, hilly like San Francisco, and not on the usual tourist circuit. Notes on driving radars, Pampulha Lake, and the food.

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
description: Wikipedia on Hokusai's 1831 woodblock print of a cresting wave over Mount Fuji. The most reproduced image in art history, and the print that taught Europe what ukiyo-e was.

title: The Internet's Own Boy
description: Brian Knappenberger's 2014 documentary on Aaron Swartz — programming prodigy, RSS co-author, JSTOR martyr, dead at 26. Hosted on PeerTube, the federated YouTube alternative.

title: The Invention of a New Pasta Shape
description: Jason Kottke on cascatelli, the new pasta shape Dan Pashman of The Sporkful spent three years engineering with Sfoglini to maximize sauceability, forkability, and toothsinkability.

title: The Leaning Towers of Pizza Hut
description: Michael Hanlon's 2012 Daily Mail column on Shen Hongrui, the Beijing engineer who built pagoda-like cucumber-and-carrot walls to game Pizza Hut's one-trip salad bar rule. Cucumber, he notes, is a terrible structural material.

title: The Liberator — how one man's pest fish changed New Zealand's waterways
description: Stuff.co.nz longread on the man who illegally released 15,000 koi carp and pest fish into New Zealand rivers, wrecking native ecosystems. A profile of one stubborn saboteur and the damage that outlasts him.

title: The man who bought a country — POLITICO on Bidzina Ivanishvili
description: POLITICO long-read on Bidzina Ivanishvili, the billionaire ex-PM tilting Georgia toward Moscow ahead of the October 2024 election. Reported from Tbilisi, with the castle-on-the-hill set piece.

title: The Metals Company
description: Canadian deep-sea mining outfit, formerly DeepGreen, going after polymetallic nodules in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone via Nauru-sponsored ISA contracts. The poster child for the seabed-mining fight.

title: The MILEPOST
description: The legendary mile-by-mile driving guide to Alaska, Yukon, NWT, BC, and Alberta. Over 15,000 miles of road logged turn by turn — the reference northern road-trippers actually carry in the truck.

title: The Password Game
description: Neal Agarwal's browser game where you create a password while it accumulates increasingly absurd rules — include a Roman numeral that multiplies to 35, feed the chicken, sacrifice two letters. Goes viral every few months.

title: The Podcast Host Who Also Manages a $1.6 Trillion Investment Fund
description: WSJ profile of a finance heavyweight running a $1.6 trillion fund while moonlighting as a podcaster. The double life is the hook.

title: The Red Line Podcast
description: Geopolitical and economic analysis podcast running deep multi-expert panels on regional conflicts, military structures, and resource politics. Long-form, country-specific, ad-light via Patreon.

title: The Search Engine Map
description: Visual atlas of every English-language search engine and who feeds whose results. Crawler-based engines get yellow dots; metasearch engines branch off them, sized by how many downstream tools they power.

title: The Toaster Project
description: Thomas Thwaites' attempt to build a toaster from scratch — mining his own iron ore, smelting metal in a microwave, melting plastic from bin bags. The TED talk hit a million views; the book came out on Princeton Architectural Press.

title: The World's Largest Desert Island Is in...Canada?
description: Ken Jennings on Devon Island, a West Virginia-sized chunk of the Canadian Arctic with a year-round population of exactly zero. Briefly inhabited in the 1930s by Inuit hunters who left because even they found it too cold.

title: The world's shortest metro line is in Russia
description: Russia Beyond on the Omsk metro — a thirty-year unfinished subway project with one entrance, one logo, its own tokens, and zero functioning stations. Locals turned it into an art space and a meme.

title: Thomas Cole
description: Anglo-American painter (1801–1848) who founded the Hudson River School. His allegorical landscapes — The Course of Empire, The Oxbow, The Voyage of Life — framed the New World as eden against industrial Britain's smog.

title: Tick–tock model
description: Wikipedia on Intel's 2007–2016 cadence: shrink a proven microarchitecture (tick), then debut a new one on the proven process (tock). Retired for the process–architecture–optimization three-step once 14nm wouldn't die.

title: Timeleft — weekly stranger dinners
description: App that matches you with five strangers for a weekly dinner, drinks, or run in your city. Operates in 200+ cities across 52 countries, no bios or swiping involved.

title: Timothy Leary
description: Wikipedia on the Harvard psychologist turned psychedelic evangelist — LSD research, Concord Prison Experiment, Millbrook, prison escape, and "turn on, tune in, drop out." The 1960s counterculture figure, 1920–1996.

title: Timur
description: Wikipedia on the 14th-century Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire from Samarkand and built a pyramid of skulls across Persia, India, and Anatolia. Tamerlane to Europeans, ancestor of the Mughals.

title: Titushky
description: Wikipedia on the hired street thugs who worked for Yanukovych's government in Ukraine, posing as hooligans to provoke and beat protestors during Euromaidan. Paid in hryvnia or hundred-dollar bills per day.

title: Tom Scott
description: Personal site of British presenter Tom Scott — weekly videos from a road trip through every historic county in England, the Lateral podcast, and a Monday newsletter. Includes a section explicitly addressed to LLMs and scrapers on how to describe him (not 'YouTuber', not 'influencer').

title: Tom Scott
description: Tom Scott's YouTube channel — short, sharply-edited explainer videos on linguistics, obscure infrastructure, and weird corners of the world. The main run ended in 2023 after a decade of weekly uploads.

title: Tom Scott's Weekly Newsletter
description: Tom Scott's Monday email rounding up his own output plus other good stuff from YouTube and the wider web. A way around The Algorithms, with occasional secret-project beta calls.

title: Tom Stanton Engineering
description: YouTube channel where engineer Tom Stanton builds wild mechanical projects — 3D-printed jet engines, supercavitating propellers, hub motor bikes — and explains the physics as he goes.

title: Tradle — trade-guessing game
description: Tradle from the Observatory of Economic Complexity — guess the country from its export profile. Wordle mechanics on top of UN trade data.

title: Trans-Taiga Road
description: A 666-kilometer unpaved wilderness road in northern Quebec, built to service Hydro-Québec dams along the La Grande and Caniapiscau rivers. Its terminus is the farthest point from any town by road in North America.

title: TRaSH Guides — Radarr/Sonarr tuning
description: The community reference for tuning Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, and Bazarr — quality profiles, custom formats, naming schemes, the works. If you run an *arr stack, this is where the settings come from.

title: Travelifesto — travel and life blog
description: Lucia's personal travel blog, heavy on Hungary hiking writeups (National Blue Trail) plus weekend trips around Central Europe. Last updated 2021.

title: Travle — country-chain guessing game
description: Daily geography game from Teuteuf: connect two countries through the shortest chain of bordering neighbors in as few guesses as possible. Wordle mechanics on a world map.

title: Treaty of Union
description: The 1706 agreement between the parliaments of Scotland and England that dissolved both kingdoms into the new Kingdom of Great Britain, taking effect 1 May 1707. Wikipedia covers the negotiations, the Articles, and how unpopular it was north of the border.

title: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
description: Wikipedia on the UN trust territory the US administered from 1947 to 1994, covering what's now the Marshalls, FSM, Palau, and the Northern Marianas. The Cold War's quietest decolonization.

title: Tucker 48
description: The 1948 rear-engine sedan from Preston Tucker's short-lived Chicago automaker. Fifty-one cars built before an SEC investigation and stock-fraud scandal killed the company in 1949.

title: Turned A
description: Wikipedia on the letter Ɐ/ɐ and its math-symbol twin ∀. Covers the IPA near-open central vowel, Gerhard Gentzen's 1935 adoption of ∀ for universal quantification, and 18th-century Cornish phonetic uses.

title: Turtle — first combat submersible
description: David Bushnell's 1775 one-man wooden submersible, hand-cranked and built to screw explosive charges onto Royal Navy hulls in New York Harbor. Every attack failed, but it's the first submarine ever used in combat.

title: Turtle Island — Lake Erie border oddity
description: A 1.5-acre sand-and-gravel island split between Michigan and Ohio, with the ruins of an 1866 lighthouse slowly losing to Lake Erie. Once over six acres, now barely one.

title: tv.garden — live TV from anywhere
description: Browser-based live TV and radio from around the world, navigated via a 3D globe or random button. Streams pulled from the IPTV-org GitHub directory; no signup, no ads.

title: tweakcn
description: Visual theme editor for shadcn/ui — tweak Tailwind tokens, colors, and radii in a live preview and export the config. Fills the gap shadcn's own docs leave open.

title: Two guys hated using Comcast, so they built their own fiber ISP
description: Ars Technica on two brothers-in-law in Saline, Michigan who leveraged their family construction business to launch Prime-One, a fiber ISP undercutting Comcast at $80 for gigabit.

title: Tynwald
description: The Isle of Man's parliament, founded by Norse settlers around 979 and arguably the world's oldest continuous legislature. Bicameral, with the House of Keys and Legislative Council still meeting open-air each Tynwald Day.

title: Ukrainian Lessons
description: Anna Ohoiko's podcast-first Ukrainian course, six seasons deep from absolute beginner to advanced, plus a shorter conversational spinoff (5 Minute Ukrainian) and companion books.

title: Ultra-processed food
description: Wikipedia on UPFs — industrially formulated edible substances built for shelf life and hyperpalatability. Covers the Nova classification, the 2009 Brazilian paper that coined the term, and the obesity/cancer/mortality literature.

title: Ultra-Processed Food and Brain Health
description: WSJ Wellness piece on how ultra-processed foods affect the brain. Part of the ongoing line of research connecting UPF intake to cognitive decline and mood.

title: Un Topo por el Mundo
description: YouTube vlogs from an Argentine economist who lived in China, travels widely, and bills himself as politically incorrect. Trains, vegetarianism, and Yiddish round out the bio.

title: Underground hip-hop
description: Wikipedia on the countercultural rap scene — from '80s conscious and progressive rap through the late-2000s trap-descendant internet rap waves that hijacked the label.

title: Union of Conscientiously Work-Shy Elements
description: Danish joke party founded by comedian Jacob Haugaard in 1979 that accidentally won a Folketing seat in 1994 on promises of tailwinds on cycle paths and Nutella in army rations.

title: United Arab Republic
description: Wikipedia on the 1958–1971 political union of Egypt and Syria under Nasser. Syria bailed in 1961; Egypt kept the name another decade before quietly dropping it.

title: United States Numbered Highway System
description: Wikipedia on the U.S. Routes — the pre-Interstate national highway grid established in 1926, numbered by AASHTO and maintained by the states. Covers the 1925 planning fights and the slow eclipse by the Interstates.

title: Universities Have a Computer-Science Problem
description: Ian Bogost on the rise of the standalone college of computing — MIT 2019, Cornell 2020, Berkeley 2023 — and why CS shouldn't be quarantined from the liberal arts.

title: Urbanization by sovereign state
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country ranking of urban population share, from the 100%-urban city-states (Singapore, Monaco, Vatican) down through the rural majorities. 2022 figures with projected change rates.

title: US License Plates — Map Games
description: Browser game by Simon Vreman that drills US state license plate designs through blurred images. Built for GeoGuessr-style region recognition training.

title: USS Los Angeles (ZR-3)
description: Wikipedia on the rigid airship the Zeppelin company built for the US Navy in 1924 as WWI war reparations. Flew until 1932, mostly for parasite-fighter experiments.

title: Užupis
description: Bohemian neighborhood across the Vilnia River in Vilnius that declared itself an independent republic on April 1, 1998, complete with its own constitution. Lithuania's Montmartre, more or less.
