title: Varieties of Chinese
description: Wikipedia's survey of the Sinitic branch — Mandarin, Yue, Wu, Min, Hakka and the rest — covering mutual unintelligibility, classification debates, and the politics of calling them dialects.

title: Vehicle registration plates of the Mercosur
description: Wikipedia on the unified license plate system rolling out across Mercosur countries. Approved in 2010 at Foz do Iguaçu, finally hitting the road around 2018 across Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay — Venezuela suspended.

title: Vela incident
description: The 1979 double flash detected by a US Vela satellite over the South Atlantic, widely read as an undeclared Israeli–South African nuclear test. Carter-era cover-up, still officially unresolved.

title: VeloPlanner
description: Trip-planning hub for the world's official signposted cycling routes — EuroVelo, Alpe Adria, Elbe, and national networks — with a route planner that prefers marked bike infrastructure.

title: Velvet Revolution
description: Wikipedia on the 1989 nonviolent uprising that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia in six weeks. Day-by-day chronology from the November 17 student march through Havel's December 29 presidency.

title: Veritasium
description: Derek Muller's science YouTube channel — physics, engineering, and counterintuitive demos shot on location with the people doing the work. Eleven million subscribers and a PhD thesis on why explainer videos work.

title: Vienna Convention on Road Traffic
description: The 1968 UN treaty standardizing road rules across 86 parties, including the framework that makes International Driving Permits work. Notably also where autonomous-vehicle law gets argued.

title: Vietnam Consolidates from 63 to 34 Provinces
description: Vietnam Briefing on the National Assembly resolution that collapses the country's 63 provinces and centrally governed cities down to 34. Business-press coverage of a major administrative redraw.

title: Vietnam's $27 Billion Death-Sentence Appeal
description: Truong My Lan, sentenced to death for swindling $27 billion from Saigon Commercial Bank, opens her appeal calling the sentence 'too severe and harsh.' One of the largest corruption cases in history.

title: Viktor Gushan
description: Wikipedia on the Transnistrian businessman and ex-KGB officer who co-founded Sheriff, the holding company that controls roughly 60% of Transnistria's economy. Nicknamed 'the Sheriff' from his KGB days.

title: Villa 31
description: Wikipedia on the Retiro slum tucked between Recoleta and the port of Buenos Aires. Forty thousand residents, mostly Paraguayan and Bolivian, on land the city spent decades trying to evict before legalizing it.

title: Virginia Tech Repository PDF
description: A PDF bitstream from VTechWorks, Virginia Tech's institutional repository. No title in the URL — could be a thesis, dissertation, technical report, or faculty paper.

title: Visa requirements for United States citizens
description: Wikipedia's country-by-country breakdown of where a US passport gets you in visa-free, visa-on-arrival, or full-visa terms. Also covers the Passport Card, EDL, and APEC Business Travel Card.

title: Volterra
description: Walled mountaintop town in Tuscany with Etruscan, Roman, and medieval bones layered on top of each other. Population around 9,000, sitting at 531 meters above the Pisa province.

title: Voter Turnout in US Presidential Elections
description: Wikipedia's overview of how turnout in US presidential races has shifted with suffrage expansions, registration policy, and demographic gaps. Includes state-by-state breakdowns from 1976 onward.

title: VW is reviving Scout to sell electric SUVs
description: CNN Business on Volkswagen spinning up a standalone US subsidiary to relaunch the Scout nameplate as an American-market electric SUV brand. Peter Valdes-Dapena, March 2024.

title: Walking 10,000+ steps daily cuts mortality in prediabetes and diabetes
description: Healio news writeup on a Diabetes Care study finding that adults with prediabetes or diabetes who walk over 10,000 steps a day have lower all-cause mortality. Short clinical summary, not the underlying paper.

title: Warsaw Pact Invasion of Czechoslovakia
description: Wikipedia on Operation Danube, the 1968 Soviet-led invasion that crushed the Prague Spring and ended Dubček's socialism-with-a-human-face experiment. Sets up the Brezhnev Doctrine and the long Normalization that followed.

title: Was Steve Jobs Right About Market Research?
description: FlexMR blog post defending traditional market research against the famous Jobs line about customers not knowing what they want. Industry-insider rebuttal from a research-tech vendor.

title: Waveform — The MKBHD Podcast
description: Marques Brownlee and Andrew Manganelli's weekly tech podcast, hosted on the Vox Media network. Long-form companion to the MKBHD YouTube reviews — phones, cameras, EVs, and what's worth your money.

title: WeatherSpark — climate averages by city
description: Detailed climate and weather averages for cities worldwide, with charts breaking down temperature, precipitation, wind, and daylight across the year. The go-to for 'what's the weather actually like in X' before a trip.

title: Wendover Productions
description: Sam Denby's explainer channel on how the world works — logistics, aviation, geopolitics, infrastructure economics. New video every other Tuesday, dense with maps and supply-chain detail.

title: Where does, or might, your streaming money go? — furialog
description: Glenn McDonald (ex-Spotify, Every Noise at Once) walks through how to model alternate streaming royalty schemes against your own Spotify listening history using his Curio query tool.

title: Where people go to bars to drink milk
description: BBC Travel dispatch from Kigali's milk bars, where Rwandans gather over ikivuguto and inshyushyu. A window into how central cows are to Rwandan culture, economy, and everyday greetings.

title: Why Sweden helped free an Australian student in North Korea
description: BBC explainer on Sweden's role as Western powers' 'protecting power' in Pyongyang, prompted by the 2019 release of student Alek Sigley. Traces the tradition back to 19th-century neutrality and the 1953 armistice commission.

title: Why time seems to pass faster as we age
description: Paras Chopra's tweetstorm-style theory that time speeds up because predictability lets the brain stop encoding new memories. Childhood feels long because everything was a surprise worth storing.

title: Wigwam Motel
description: The tipi-shaped motel chain Frank Redford built along the American roadside in the 1930s–40s. Three of the original seven villages survive, two of them on Route 66.

title: WikiChip
description: Wiki dedicated to chips, semiconductors, and computer architecture. Deep reference for CPU microarchitectures, instruction sets, and silicon history — the kind of detail Wikipedia tends to flatten.

title: Wikiexplora — South American trekking route guide
description: Joaquín Barañao's wiki of 1,300+ trekking, climbing, and mountain-bike routes across Chile, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia, Colombia, and Ecuador. Born from a Santiago mountaineer's overflowing bookshelf.

title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
description: Wikipedia editors' field guide to spotting LLM-generated articles — the canned emphasis, em-dash overuse, fake DOIs, and giveaway artifacts like 'turn0search0' links. A living taxonomy from the front lines of the slop war.

title: Will Tennyson
description: YouTube channel from fitness creator Will Tennyson — bodybuilding experiments, calorie-counting stunts, and eat-like-an-athlete day-in-the-life videos. Approachable gym-bro content with a comedic edge.

title: Wimpy — British burger chain
description: French Wikipedia on Wimpy, the British fast-food chain born in 1930s Chicago and named after Popeye's burger-obsessed sidekick. Jacques Borel brought it to Paris in 1961 as France's first fast-food restaurant.

title: Wiphala
description: The seven-color square patchwork flag representing Andean indigenous peoples across Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, and beyond. Made a co-official national symbol of Bolivia in 2009 alongside the tricolor.

title: Withdrawal of Greenland from the European Communities
description: Wikipedia on how Greenland left the EC in 1985, twelve years after joining as part of Denmark. A 53% withdrawal vote in 1982, formalized by the Greenland Treaty — the only territory to ever exit before Brexit.

title: Wojtek — Polish Army's soldier bear
description: Syrian brown bear bought from an Iranian shepherd in 1942, enlisted as a corporal in the 2nd Polish Corps, and carried ammunition crates at Monte Cassino. Retired to Edinburgh Zoo.

title: Wonderful Wadis — Oman's Vertical Desert
description: Lonely Planet feature on Oman's wadis, the steep canyon oases cutting through the Hajar mountains. Pitched as a 'vertical desert' angle on the country's water-carved interior.

title: Wooden Skyscrapers Are on the Rise
description: WSJ piece on the mass-timber boom — engineered wood replacing steel and concrete in tall buildings, with developers betting on lower carbon and faster builds.

title: Workaway
description: Work-exchange platform pairing travelers with hosts in 170+ countries — help out on a farm, hostel, or family home in exchange for food and a bed. The dominant player in the volunteer-travel niche, alongside WWOOF and Worldpackers.

title: World Nomad Games
description: Biennial international competition for ethnic sports of Central Asia — eagle hunting, horseback wrestling, the works. Founded in Kyrgyzstan in 2014; 37 sports, 70+ countries, billed as the Olympics for nomadic peoples.

title: World-first study reveals the mysteries of the marsupial mole
description: Popular Science on the first DNA study of Australia's marsupial moles — tiny, pencil-sized desert mammals that 'swim' through sand and are sighted only a few times per decade.

title: Writing as a Form of Thinking
description: Pedro Lopes on what gets lost when you hand the writing process to an LLM. The text is the byproduct; the thinking happens in the drafting.

title: Y Wladfa
description: Wikipedia on the Welsh colony in Patagonia, founded 1865 along the Chubut Valley to preserve language and chapel culture far from English encroachment. Patagonian Welsh still survives in pockets of Chubut Province.

title: Yahoo Answers
description: Wikipedia on Yahoo's community Q&A site, mocked for years over its question quality before shutting down in May 2021. The /r/answers chum bucket of the 2000s web.

title: Yakuza
description: Wikipedia on Japan's organized crime syndicates — their 17th-century kabukimono origins, internal rituals, designated-bōryokudan legal status, and overseas footprints from São Paulo to Honolulu.

title: Yes Theory
description: YouTube channel built on the slogan 'seek discomfort' — four friends chasing absurd challenges, stranger encounters, and impulsive trips. Spawned a merch line and a sizable subculture around saying yes.

title: Yes Theory
description: YouTube channel from the Yes Theory crew, built on the slogan 'seek discomfort' — stunt-driven travel and social-experiment videos pushing strangers and themselves out of their comfort zones.

title: Yevgeny Zamyatin
description: Russian novelist and naval engineer (1884–1937) who wrote We, the dystopia that pre-dates and shaped Orwell and Huxley. Bolshevik turned dissident, died in Paris exile.

title: Yugo
description: Wikipedia on the Zastava Yugo, the Yugoslav subcompact built in Kragujevac from 1980 to 2008. Punchline of a thousand car jokes after its disastrous 1985 US launch under Malcolm Bricklin.

title: Yungas
description: The narrow band of cloud forest down the eastern slope of the Andes, running from Peru through Bolivia into northwest Argentina. Transitional zone between Andean highlands and the Amazon basin — Aymara and Quechua both named it for the warmth.

title: Yunnan
description: Wikipedia on China's southwestern province bordering Myanmar, Laos, and Vietnam. Mountainous, ethnically diverse — 25 recognized minorities — and the historical seat of the Dian, Nanzhao, and Dali kingdoms before Yuan absorption.

title: Zach Star Himself
description: Zach Star's secondary YouTube channel, where the math-and-engineering explainer drops the lesson plan for sketches, rants, and whatever he feels like making that week.

title: zi8gzag — YouTube channel
description: YouTube channel @zi8gzag. No page content available; identity and subject matter unknown from the URL alone.

title: Zinaida Portnova
description: Soviet teenage partisan who poisoned a German garrison's food in occupied Belarus before being captured and killed at 17. Posthumous Hero of the Soviet Union, immortalized on a 1978 stamp.
